title: My expectations were high but i was still quite disappointed
body:
I really appreciate the concept of Habitica, and I believe gamification could greatly help me in achieving my goals. However, I feel a bit disappointed because the minigames aren't very engaging and seem disconnected from the tasks. When I complete a task, I only feel satisfaction from the task itself, as I don't find the pets or boss fights particularly interesting. While these features help keep me somewhat accountable, they don't add much excitement.

I suggest adding an extra step between completing a task and earning rewards, such as a short text-based adventure that players can experience after finishing a task. Introducing more minigames, perhaps similar to the Discord meme game, could enhance the fun factor, as it aligns with the style Habitica aims for. Additionally, crafting systems for creating better weapons and armor, and allowing pets to provide buffs, could add depth to the game.

For the boss fights, incorporating more prominent character synergies that are effective against certain bosses would make them more strategic and engaging. Overall, I think Habitica has tremendous potential to be useful, but in its current state, it feels similar to other to-do list apps. That being said i still use habitica and find it useful

title: Fantastic - bordering on life-changing
body:
I could not run my life without this app. That's the shortest possible way I can describe my experience with it after using it for three years. It's cute and fun and its structure grasps something that few other task management apps have been able to replicate. Separating habits, periodical tasks and one-off to-do's is simple but like many simple things, it took a long time for somebody to do it! Now that Habitica has, though, there's no going back for me. 

Recent updates have introduced some annoying bugs but the developers are responsive and hard-working. I'm sure they'll iron them out quickly as they always do. The glitches are worth putting up with, especially because you can use Habitica in a browser, where there are few glitches. The browser use means that you can have it open in a tab on your computer at work, in class or anywhere else and not have to worry about using your phone.

This thing is just so versatile. It only loses a star because some of its current bugs are a bit of a hassle. Let me repeat myself, though: they are worth putting up with for this gem of an app.

title: Review v2.1.2 (2/XII/2018)
body:
This app has come a long way since its inception. Version 2.0 was the biggest leap forward for this app, having introduced a whole lot more stability and functionality than previously. 

It's true that v2.0.0 was still buggy, but upon reflection, it was hard to expect them to get it perfect...because they aren't as big as Google or Facebook. Big mistakes were bound to appear left, right and centre.

While the issues with synchronisation are still there, it's pretty good with conflict resolution between tasks as far as I can tell. The app is much more stable and there is a fair amount of functionality regarding feeding pets and starting Quests. (Still need to fix up the bug where it takes multiple refreshes to view the quest details and buttons without distortion.)

All in all, this app is a good supplement to the main website, but they do need to step up their game if they want their game to capture the essence of productivity in us all.

title: Lots of Room for Improvement
body:
Hopefully creators will read this, I am genuinely interested to use the app to its fullest potential and will be interested to support the app after a few more weeks of using it.

My thoughts on first glance:

Ideas:

1. Changing the title for ‘Dailies’, i think something like Recurring Tasks or just Tasks would make more sense considering there’s the option to have Daily, Monthly and Yearly reminders.

2. Need more details for Reminders. Currently the reminders for tasks only come in time (e.g. 8:00am) but tasks that continue for a few days might need more advanced detail such as reminders in multiple times during the day (morning, afternoon, night). Or needing to be reminded a few hours, days or minutes before a task.

3. Option to colour code tasks when they’re created.

4. Option to add custom tags.

Bugs:

1. The Character inside the Profile Picture is a little off-centre

2. Slide bar to delete tasks take too long to delete the task, or loading problem when task is being deleted.

title: App of the year!
body:
Habitrpg has been the most useful app I have downloaded all year. As a sufferer of anxiety, I often battle with a consistent buzzing in my head which makes me unable to remember things I should do in a day. When the day finishes, I go to bed with a sense of unfulfilment, wondering if I forgot anything today. This brought me to a place where I would lose track of my studying and lose sleep because of last minute assignments. The stress of this was causing health complications. 

Ever since I got habitrpg, I have been able to keep a step-by-step record of my tasks, and good habits are much more inviting and memorable when I can add points for them. I check my to-do list and my dailys every night and I get a sense of peace because I know what I have done that day. Habitrpg is not only a fantastic program to boost your good habits and prune the bad habits, but it is also an amazing way to keep track of a stressful life.

title: I Don't Write Reviews
body:
Ever. So why am I starting now? Because I use Habit RPG frequently and have always been frustrated by the lack of features in their app.

Never again will I have to say that.

For those people who don't know: Habit RPG is a task-keeper; a to-do-list and a tiny bundle of sprite based, quest induced joy. This is their app.

It supports all the features available at the full Habit RPG website and has been cleverly formatted to, very successfully, work on your phone or other iOS device with minimal effort on your part.

The app itself feels well developed and polished, additionally it is hands down my favourite To-do-list on iOS.

Cheers. 

DIE CHECKLIST. DIE.

I was a bit sad to see that the volunteers and the core team had a dispute. There seems to be no volunteers now. I also wished Habitica is a non profit since many volunteers worked on it and I do love non profit open source softwares.
The app is still very nice although there has been less updates to the quest and new items these few years. The app is still very useful and is worth a try.

title: exactly what i wanted
body:
i was thinking to myself, “i wish there was an app that would make a game out of my todo list,” and then i was pondering how i might teach myself to code just to make said app, when i realized that i have never had an original thought so the app definitely exists— a google search, download, and some time later, and im here giving 5 stars to a phenomenally executed and wonderful concept. 

only downside is i hate the ponytail hairstyle lol. but this app is!!! i have already had todo lists and task lists my entire life, but to gamify it all is a fun + rewarding way to ensure i feel like i “want” to do the sidequests (my chores).

I was recommended this app by my therapist, and the customization of the to-do’s and dailies helps me remember small tasks like remembering to brush my teeth. The to-do list is good to help
me remember homework, since I have no object permanence when it comes to assignments. 

However, the app does have some small issues, since the widgets have a weird border, and one time, after completing a quest, I had roughly 1030 XP out of 440 required to level up. This glitch fixed itself after I marked a daily off, and shot me from Level 20 to Level 22. 

The game also has a lovely community, as everyone’s working to be a better version of themselves to some degree. 

Overall, keeps me productive, but has some smaller issues that understandably could be a dealbreaker for some.

title: Clean interface but lack of updates
body:
I've loved using this app for years and years, and it genuinely helped motivate me to start healthy habits for the better. It's simple but effective, has a clean interface, and the separate tabs for habits/daily tasks/one-off to-dos is so much easier to navigate than other apps that throw them all together in one list. The paid gems & premium subscriptions are pretty reasonable too - free players get full functionality and paid players can buy quests for extra cosmetics or host challenges.

On the downside, the app's had few content updates and once you run out of free quests there's not much left to work towards besides those monetized cosmetics. The community aspect has also wound down - with staff alienating the volunteer mods in a messy situation - so the guilds and chatrooms were shut down too. I learned so much from the supportive communities there, so that social aspect is sorely missed.

TLDR: Good app that could use content updates and a reinvigorated social scene.

The app still has a Looking for Group feature, and the Tavern and some of the guilds have migrated to unofficial Discords, but this shutdown of social spaces is not a good sign of things to come.

title: Pleasantly surprised
body: I have ADHD, and a classic trait of ADHD is that while constantly picking up new healthy habits, like keeping a new agenda or setting alarms for tasks etc. is necessary and good, it’s also sort of futile because no matter what, an ADHDer is always going to lapse and drop said habit — which, hey, whatever, just pick it up again and keep trekking on! But it’s still such a discouraging cycle… but Habitica is the first of these new healthy habits I’ve picked up and maintained so easily for such a long stretch of time. It’s genuinely fun! In order to fight monsters and get sick new loot, you HAVE to check into the app, confirm that you’ve done your homework or your chores or you’ve brushed your teeth… what an awesome idea. Oh, and it has tons of “guilds” and “parties” to join which are essentially just fun little clubs focusing on topics from your favourite TV shows to mental health support. The app has minor flaws, sure, and it would be cool if the art and customization features were more elaborate in the future, but Habitica executes this idea decently well and I have nothing to be mad about :)

Second, I like to see my tasks on my phone home screen, but because of the first error the widget only showed the message “Start your day”. I’ve decided to use a similar app, but if these errors are fixed, I shall come back. I like their party/guild system where I can communicate with other ADHD people, and encourage each other.

title: 3 month Review
body:
I’m an Autism/ADHD Support Service Provider and University Student. I’ve been using this daily for 3 months with one of my students (We formed a party).
Here is what it has helped me with:

- Organization
- Positive reinforcement for mundane tasks
- Daily Accountability (And some competitiveness)
- An awesome way to reward my students for assignments that need to be done via “Gems”.
- Reframing schoolwork as “Challenges” instead of..  work.
- Found a fun community (Guild) for people using the Forrest App, which has increased my Forest App usage and productivity tremendously!
- Given me a good way to measure my success as I grind through the first year of a CS degree online. 
- Allowed me to be a kid again.

Here is what it hasn’t helped me with:
- A drive to succeed in life
- It hasn’t magically fixed my problems

All in all, I really enjoy the app and will continue to use it as there is tons to achieve in-game despite being 3 months in. My student and I bond over it, and he actually does homework for gems which is a miracle in itself. The Resource Teacher is impressed, his Mom is stoked, and my student is getting things done. I bought 60 gems for $10 (sale) which I expect to last us both a year in challenges.

Big thanks to the Habitica team for creating such a fun idea and for helping people everywhere get things done. Amazing what some imagination and hard work can do. Cheers.

title: Super fun way to better habits!
body:

Or, you can just do your own thing and be rewarded for your progress (though there are certain aspects of the game that you won’t be able to access alone - like going on quests). I personally feel that some interaction makes for more accountability anyway. Most of the people that I have been sharing a party with are wonderfully supportive, though I have never met them IRL. 

For a few things, the website is much easier to access (Orb of Rebirth, setting pets and mounts free from the stable). But for the most part, these are things that are done more rarely. 

In my time on Habitica, the game has improved a lot and they are always adding new things and fixing any bugs. Shout out to all of those working to always make it better. 

Everything you need to know about how to get the most out of this app is written out in a Fandom Wiki. So, if you are going to really get into it, look for that to find out about all of the great features and how to use them.

I want to see right in front of me, everyday, how many days I've succeeded in doing that task. Just a simple line under each task showing the days of the month that you finished the task. title: Changed my life
body:
Finally, a productivity app that's actually motivating!

Habitica's Life-as-an-RPG approach to motivation, combined with the fully flexible structure that lets you customize to YOUR goals and aspirations really worked wonders for the nerd in me! I eyeball different pets and armour sets, and force myself to stick to my resolutions and practice my new habits so I can get that gold and XP so I can buy them! The endless variety of sets makes sure it's not only customizable, but that you'll be hard pressed to collect it all. 

The quests system really ties it all together; after all there's no point in buying a better sword if you've nothing to swing it at! And the social setup is flexible enough that you can play with IRL friends, or make new ones through the app! Very well moderated too so you don't have to worry about chat harassment. 

5/5 would definitely recommend. I love imagining 'Habiteer-Me' getting a power boost from Normal Me's everyday work. Makes normal chores so much more fun!

title: Good idea!
body:
Feature Suggestion: Completed To-Dos History

Hello Habitica team and community! 👋

I would like to suggest adding a “Completed To-Dos History” feature to Habitica.

🔹 What is it?

A section or tab where users can view their completed To-Dos, showing the task name, completion date, and rewards earned (XP and gold).

🔹 Why is it useful?
	•	Helps users track and reflect on what they’ve accomplished.
	•	Useful for reusing or reactivating important tasks from the past.
	•	Motivates users by showing their progress and efforts.
	•	Could assist with productivity reviews or personal analytics.

🔹 Bonus Ideas (Optional Features):
	•	Filters by date, difficulty, or tags.
	•	Option to restore a completed To-Do as a new task.
	•	List or calendar view of completed To-Dos.

Thanks for considering this! I believe it would really improve the experience and sense of accomplishment in Habitica. 🗒️✨

title: Ist in Ordnung
body: Nach meinem Test der Habitica-App bin ich insgesamt sehr zufrieden mit ihrer Funktionalität und dem motivierenden Gamification-Ansatz. Die Verbindung von Aufgabenmanagement mit spielerischen Elementen funktioniert überzeugend und kann wirklich helfen, den Alltag produktiver zu gestalten. Allerdings sind mir zwei Aspekte aufgefallen, die noch optimiert werden könnten: Zum einen wirkt die Benutzeroberfläche recht unübersichtlich – gerade für neue Nutzer kann die Vielzahl an Funktionen und die komplexe Menüführung eine gewisse Einstiegshürde darstellen. Besonders die Abgrenzung zwischen „Gewohnheiten“, „täglichen Aufgaben“ und „To-Dos“ ist anfangs nicht ganz selbsterklärend. Eine klarere Struktur und bessere Einführung würden hier sicher weiterhelfen. Zum anderen kam es während meines Tests vereinzelt zu kleineren technischen Problemen, etwa Verzögerungen in der Reaktion der App. Auch ein Offline-Modus fehlt bislang, was die Nutzung unterwegs ohne stabile Verbindung etwas einschränkt.

title: Two suggestions - love it besides that
body:
I recently found this app and I really love it, as I haven’t been this consequent about chores for over a month ever. 💛

I have two minor things that need a little fixing though: 

1. in the daily tab when I tick off things that go for example every 7 days: sometimes I do them a few days before because I was able to and the counter doesn’t reset, so it pops up the next day seeming like it is due, even though it is already done. In other words I want to be able to water my plants roughly every seven days, not exactly every seven days and ONLY on the seventh day. 

2. also in the dailies tab for tasks that don’t go every day. When I don’t tick them off exactly the day they pop up, they disappear instead of staying due. This really bugs me because my plants still need water and me being reminded about it, even though I didn’t manage the day before

Hope this makes sense and I would really appreciate if this would be fixed - or at least the option to set it this way.

title: Inzwischen nicht mehr empfehlenswert
body: Habitica hat einige nette Grundfunktionen, aber etliche Sachen funktionieren nur auf der Website. Trotz etlicher Beschwerden wurde daran in den letzten Jahren nichts geändert. Überhaupt wurde wenig Neues hinzugefügt, nur (zugegebenermaßen schöne) Deko. Was immer toll war, war die Community. Die (ehrenamtlichen) Moderatoren haben echt gute Arbeit geleistet, und viele Leute haben tolle Herausforderungen erstellt. Die Moderatoren wurden gefeuert, durften sich nicht verabschieden, es ist verboten, in Habitica selbst darüber zu reden. Die Mitarbeiter von Habitica sind nicht nur nicht in der Lage, sondern auch nicht willens, weiter eine positive und sichere Umgebung herzustellen. Stattdessen ist der Hauptchat (Taverne) jetzt oft zugespammt und beinhaltet triggernde Themen. Deshalb verlassen etliche der engagierten und erfahrenen Spieler gerade Habitica. Es ist leider nicht mehr empfehlenswert. :-(

title: Used Habitica for 7 years, can no longer recommend it
body:
As the title says, I have been using Habitica for 7 years - 7.5 years to be correct. 
While it’s a fairly good task manager, the lack of new features and bug fixes has made me use it less and less. What kept me there was the community, but that community is now slowly disintegrating, as all the volunteer mods have been removed. Staff has taken over moderation, and it would be a pity to say that they are even doing the bare minimum - because they certainly are not. 
So if you are looking for a supportive community, I would look elsewhere. 

Additionally, long term users and volunteer contributors are now being told off for flagging triggering content. This never happened with the volunteer mod team. It has not been possible to get clear guidelines from staff for 1.5 months. 

If you are just looking for a basic, free task manager, sure. But be aware that there have been app-breaking bugs for a long time, that seems like is no priority to fix. Just as an example, the app frequently crashes if you click any of your notifications leading to a party or guild. It is super annoying.
author: Lalaith93

title: A great To-do list with some fun on top
body:
Habitica is essentially a To-do list with a very non-intrusive RPG game slapped on top of it. The division of lists into three separate categories (Habits, Dailies and To-Dos) makes a lot of sense. It's intuitive to use and fun to look at. You can make little encouraging notes under your tasks and set difficulties (this is mostly for the previously mentioned RPG game part of it).

It has a bit of jank here and there, I've experienced some slow load, especially on the daily reset, but it's obviously being worked on AND it's a fully featured To-do app, no monthly premiums for "Habitica Gold Features".

I would highly recommend Habitica, even if you aren't a huge video game liker. The UI makes sense, it's fun to look at and apparently there's a large and supportive community in the chat section of the game.

The community - through optional multiple guilds - supply inspiration too  with challenges for different interests that you may choose to join. Challenges adds a set of habits, dailies and to- dos. I am most happy about having joined the Habitica numbers, looking forward to see future developement on the app.

title: Meilleur application pour suivie d’habitudes
body:
Habitica est de loin l’application de suivi des habitudes la plus motivante que j’ai pu essayer. Là où beaucoup d’applications se contentent de cocher des cases et d’afficher quelques graphiques, Habitica transforme réellement les tâches du quotidien en une aventure RPG. Gagner de l’expérience, monter de niveau, débloquer de l’équipement et progresser avec son personnage rend le processus beaucoup plus ludique et engageant.

Ce que j’apprécie particulièrement, c’est la possibilité de créer ses propres récompenses personnalisées. On peut définir des cadeaux ou des plaisirs adaptés à ses envies et les “acheter” avec l’or gagné en accomplissant ses tâches. Cette liberté permet de construire un système de motivation parfaitement adapté à ses objectifs personnels.

L’application est également très flexible et permet de gérer aussi bien les habitudes, les tâches ponctuelles que les routines quotidiennes.

Mes seuls regrets concernent l’absence de véritables tableaux statistiques permettant de suivre son évolution sur le long terme, ainsi que la difficulté de mettre en place certaines routines hebdomadaires. Par exemple, créer une tâche à effectuer une seule fois par semaine tout en la faisant apparaître clairement dans le widget n’est pas aussi simple qu’on pourrait l’espérer.

Malgré ces quelques points perfectibles, Habitica reste pour moi la référence des applications de suivi des habitudes grâce à son approche unique, ludique et extrêmement motivante.

title: Bon concept, mais à travailler
body:
Le concept est top et les débuts dans l’appli sont amusants. Cependant cette application souffre de deux défauts qui font que je la desinstalle après un mois d’utilisation :
- la synchronisation via internet perturbe les modifications réalisées sur les rappels. Je passe 10 minutes à me créer des rappels pour des choses importantes, des échéances, les listes de validation associées, etc, je quitte l’appli, et lorsque j’y reviens... Toutes mes modifs ont été perdues. La synchronisation ne s’est pas faite, manque de pot pour moi.
- les menus sont fort compliqués à comprendre et très fouillis (également a cause de la traduction en français peu précise) : les éléments sont tous les uns à la suite des autres, sans hiérarchie, on ne comprend pas forcément leur but lorsqu’on ne les connaît pas, et la documentation est écrite en petit et est très dense. 
Les Tutos du début sont très (trop ?) détaillés, et lorsque le contenu est plus complexe, on n’est plus suffisamment guidé.

Malgré ces défauts, le concept est bon. Lorsqu’ils seront améliorés, je retéléchargerai l’application avec plaisir.

title: It’s nearly there
body:
I love this concept of getting xp for tasks and there being an incentive to being productive for people that struggle with productivity. 

I just wish there was a big skills list for YOU as a person as well as the character you make in game. 

I could be really motivated to go gym and tick those off dailies repeatedly but neglect coursework and still feel like I’m being relatively rewarded just because xp is universal to the character. I feel like the skill tree idea that is implemented in the “Become Fearless” is a great idea to add to help people identify skills they’re good at and ones they’d benefit from working on.

This would also be a great idea for people that want to “gamify” their life a bit more than just get XP for a character, although I can see how that’s a fun gimmick, I personally want to feel like the character myself.

See games like Old School RuneScape for a better example on the different skills layout and how players earn XP to skills. 

You could have a  section when adding dailies and ToDo lists that add a checkbox on what skills you think each daily or ToDo would go towards up to 5, how important it is to be achieved and from that importance level out of 100 you can make people allocate, how much XP should go into each category that relates to it.

Just would love to give this a 5 star and I think that’s what’s missing.

body:

All this is somewhat let down by technical issues. Marking tasks and habits as done is weirdly inconsistent, especially after first opening the app. Some habits might register as being done twice and others not at all. Colour-coding of activities seems wrong sometimes (why is a habit I’ve not done showing green?). None of the problems are deal-breakers and I still use the app. But they are stopping me recommending it to others.

And bosses don’t that challenging when you complete all dailies. I feel like the game needs more content and stuff to do/complete/unlock to make it consistently rewarding even at higher levels. Perhaps something like dungeons with exclusive rewards which require a certain amount of tasks to be done in a limited time or in one day to open doors, or a certain number of habits. Maybe some animations and backgrounds could be cool too when you deal damage to a boss, to make the game more stimulating. I really do love the concept and think it can be very successful if you struggle with productivity, but i feel more can be done to gamify it further to make doing tasks just as rewarding as a video game.

title: Amazing app
body:
I never write reviews for apps but this is a really really funky concept for an app to be honest. I love games, especially ones where I can level up, gain experience, have my own avatar & generally feel like I’m being rewarded for my efforts

My psychology is really weird, when I compete a task normally, I don’t get any gratification from it instantly, example, going to the gym, but I’m still not ripped yet lol. By going to the gym now, I can actually gain experience for doing it which makes me feel like I have been rewarded for doing it, thus making we want to do it again

I’ve only had the app for a couple of days but I love it, I’m going to continue using it, invite some friends to I keep myself accountable & try to make the most out of it!

I would recommend to anyone who just  struggles to find the motivation to do something, I’ve been a long lover of games since I was a kid (and I will be for many many many more years to come) and it’s just something about this app that does it for me, it’s pleasant, user friendly & really well presented. 

All of the reviews you see about the app being “buggy” or “glitchy”, I’ve not encountered any bugs or glitches as of yet, everything worked incredibly well!

Thanks Habitica!

title: Excellent concept, but too buggy to be reliable.
body:

However, in its current state the app is too buggy for use. I had a large amount of sub-tasks that I had written to help me compartmentalise my life in order to make my depression more bearable and my life more fun. When I saved these items which took me at least an hour to write, the app crashed and deleted the item. This was devastating for me, and caused me a great deal of distress. 

The art style is excellent, but I feel like quite a lot of the cosmetic features being placed behind a gem system is an odd design choice that I don’t understand. If this system was better explained I would have had a better time with this app.

Other than that, it’s Phloorless.

title: Bugged - what happened here?
body:
I’ve used this app before without any problems and it worked fine, but after a year or so I come back and it’s really annoying.

It seems like you can’t actually delete things. I tried deleting items in a checklist because something happened where I had to move tasks to sifferent days, but qhen I hit the ⛔️ (remove) button, nothing happened as if it was just a picture. I tried removing the text in the checklist item but that didn’t do anything either, just an empty task.

Seeing as deleting a checklist task didn’t work, I tried deleting the whole task to start again but nothing happened after several attempts. I went to the help section in case I was doing something wrong. Went back to my dailies tab and several of my dailies, not just the trouble one, had disappeared, presumingly having been deleted when I tried deleting the first daily.

I can’t be bothered to use an app that can’t edit checklists and doesn’t remove a task without from the tab immediately after it’s deleted. Plus if a checklist has say 10 items, I’m not gonna bother trying to delete the whole thing and start again. It takes up the time I’m trying to put to good use with this app. 

It was a great idea that worked for me in the past but for some reason is broken now. I’m only giving it 3 stars because it used to work for me and it helped me a lot in the past with studying and taking my medication. I know it’s capable of being better.

If I hadn’t already had a good experience with the app, it would be 2 stars for sure.

Weirdly the gamifying side of Habitica became just as negatively addictive as other mobile games. Sucking into my routine and taking my attention away from a single task I needed to focus on.

Time is precious and I've become more and more conscious that apps can be a double edged sword. I'm using a regular calendar method to keep on track more with vastly better results.

Sorry Habitica, your app was brilliant to start with but the constant online status and messing about trying to get online just wasn't worth it!

title: Useful and funny
body:
The app does a fantastic job in helping you building good habits. The structure is almost perfect: you can divide your activities in three clusters. Habits, objectives and dailies. In this way, you can keep track of different kind of activities. 
On the other hand, the app lacks of two features. Firstly, I would lack to see a “recap” of my habits: maybe, a colorful calendar would help me see which days I missed my tasks.
Moreover, it would be interesting an option to have activities for an agenda.
These two options keep Habitica away from being perfect, but the app is awesome anyway.

 The first point is the option of the character icon OFF mode at the top. 
The app is very useful and I can't let go of, and I want to use it to check the routine of work, but it seems like I'm playing a game because of the top picture. Originally, I am well aware that the game element is the most important point, but could you please install a option to hide the character icon? 

 The second point is the request to shorten the time of restart when the task is carried over to the next day. When there are a lot of accomplishment tasks that I didn't check the day before, and when the game is over, the time lag until I start checking the routine of the day is long and troublesome. Originally, this is also an element that gives us the thrill of survival or death, so I understand you can't omit this process easily. However, it is stressful to have a waiting time on a busy morning.
Therefore, would it be possible for you to add a setting that reduces the time from checking the tasks left the previous day to starting the task check today? 

Thank you for your consideration.

title: 毎日チェックして遊んでます😊
body:
日常をゲームのように楽しめる大好きなタスク管理アプリです。先日のアップデートで日本語対応してますます使いやすくなりました！ いつもやる日課や思いついたTodoをタスクとして登録してます。タスクをこなすとゴールドや経験値がたまっていき、アイテムを買えたりレベルが上がったりします。ときには卵を発見してペットを孵すこともできます。私は空飛ぶブタがお気に入りです🐷💭

このアプリのおかげで自堕落な日常が変わりました。今はパーティの仲間とのんびりクエストを遊ぶのが楽しいです♪  タスクをこなすと敵にダメージを与えられて、倒すと報酬がもらえます。ゲームとしてはごくシンプルですが、コツコツこなすのが楽しいから毎日タスクをチェックするようになって、生活管理がすごく楽になりました。私のように、先延ばし・忘れもの・生活リズムの乱れで悩んでいる人はぜひ使ってみてほしいです。レトロなドット絵のゲームが好きな人にもおすすめです👾

「日本語話者の集会所」というギルドに日本人ユーザーが多くいるので、使っていて分からないことはそこで質問すれば親切な方が教えてくれます。
新しいクエストやアイテムのアップデートも定期的にあって、これからもずっと使い続けたいアプリです^_^

title: Makes tasks fun
body:
I never write reviews on apps but I like this app so much, and highly recommend it. If your life is chaotic, if your tasks are boring, if you find it hard to take control over your life or struggle with ADHD, this is the app for you. 

You can categorise your tasks into dailies, to do’s and habits. There is lots of attention to detail within the app. You create a little character which makes it fun. You can turn your life into a little game to whatever extent you want. 

I wasn’t aware of the quests and pets you could get only until much later and now I enjoy doing that too.

There’s a lot of positive things to say about this about, but the best way to find out is by downloading it and discover for yourself.

title: It used to be good, but no longer
body:
Habitica had a great thing through which you could meet others while improving your habits, all of this was mainly kept up by volunteers. But recently the company changed goals and kicked out all volunteers, that helped translate, design, help out nee members -you name it-. Ever since the social aspect has been more and more muted. Two weeks ago all guilds were shut down, though the guilds were the places where you could meet like minded people to for a party. This is no longer possible. Habitica now misses the thing that made it unique. I cancelled my subscription and left the place. I now meet my former fellow-Habiticans in other places. And I’m using another habit tracker. 

Still I hope that the company will change its mind and start listening to users instead of giving them the silent treatment and blocking people trying to reach out.

title: Beter dan de rest
body:
De app combineert verschillende manieren om je gewoonten te verbeteren waar andere apps maar 1 aspect bieden. 
Helaas is de interface wel op meerdere plekken voor verbetering vatbaar. 
Zo kun je bij jouw dagelijkse/ wekelijkse taken niet zien op welke dag je bent. Je loopt zomaar een paar dagen achter. Ook kun je niet skippen. Stel je vergeet je taak een dag, dan kun je dat niet registreren. Je moet afvinken om door te kunnen. Voor een app die je moet proberen iets aan te leren is dat raar. Het lukt immers niet in één keer om een gewoonte aan te leren. 
Ook kun je de todo lijst niet sorteren op prioriteit, staat standaard alleen op aanmaakdatum. 
Bij de gewoonten tracker kun je niet zien wat de geschiedenis is en of je deze nu wel of niet al had aangetikt. 
Wat mij betreft ligt de focus net iets teveel op het spelletje wat er inzit ipv op de gewoonten

title: De RPG voor real life quests
body:
Heel eerlijk, ik ben echt al sinds 2012
Op zoek naar een leuke manier om to do lijsten af te maken en echt motivatie te creëren voor de taken te voltooien. 
Toen speelde ik world of warcraft en heb ik regelmatig gesprekken gehad over quests voor real life taken. Zelfs een tijdje scrollen geschreven voor to do taken met een passend reward, maar nooit echt gevonden wat ik zocht.

En toen vond ik dit, brilliant en hoogmotiverend.
Erg blij met deze RPG task manager.

Ik zou t wel geweldig vinden als de quests en bossfights iets levendiger worden met iets meer interactie.
Zoiezo om taken gedaan te krijgen, de beloningen voor de taken en productiviteit vooruitgang, een hele dikke pluim!

title: Turn your To-Do list into a game
body:
Habitica makes your To-Do list fun by turning it into a game. Getting more things done in real life helps you to battle bosses, earn rewards and grow the little avatar.

The app itself is fairly buggy and could have more features hence only three stars. The features of the actual To-Do list are also less sophisticated than other apps and systems out there. 

However, it is functional enough to provide the basics and with some customisation can be tailored to suit different needs. The game aspect also helps to provide extra motivation to do a task you're on the fence about.

title: The App Bugging Out for DAYS
body:
There are entire days where the app would not respond to my updates and would revert my changes even after multiple tries. This happened for a couple of days where I re-tried checking off my daily activities and progresses and it would revert those changes as invalid. 

This is really bad because since this happened, I have not touched this app for a couple weeks and completely forgot about it. The app’s functionality is important because you’re trying to build habits to your users. If these features aren’t working at all, then there is no merit to opening the app, and therefore negates the entire point of this product. 

I imagine I’m not the only user that went back to the old habits once this app stopped working.

Better stick to a journal until they figure out a way to make this product stable.

title: Great app
body:
Things I like about the app:
1. Free and not restricting any of its features to just paid customers. I love that there’s no limit on how many habits, dallies and todos free users can create. 
2. Gamification of habits and todos really helped me become more productive.
3. Party, quest and challenges these things helped me meet new people and created a healthy competitive environment. 

Some suggestions:
1. Add a calendar that shows streaks/misses for dallies and habits.
2. On the todos page add a categories folder for all, completed and not completed todo items. Put the folders on top of the page and the todo items on the bottom.
3. Don’t delete todo items even when the deadline has been reached instead store them in folders classified as completed or not completed to show the user an overview of their progress.
4. Bring back the guild this was very useful for finding people with similar goals and interests. This feature helps people compete with other people that have similar goals, it’s also a wonderful place to communicate with people, learn and share productivity hacks and tips.

title: Good Concept, great elements…but misses the sense of urgency
body:
Hello!

I’ve been on and off Habitica for the past years and I must say that the idea and the message that the app is trying to convey is fantastic: being able to make of habits a game where you can level up and show off gear, collectibles and many, many more!

However…I feel like things are missing. Sure, the app is easy to BEGIN to use, but not rewarding enough to KEEP using it. I don’t know, I just don’t find myself coming back to Habitica week in and week out, excited as to what else there is to do. Sometimes I feel the options and features from the habit forming itself are…kind off generic.

Checklists, some pre-set coins, experience that you cannot control, that sort of stuff that is just not customizable enough. Which makes me not be able to really make my OWN economy and see how much everything REALLY costs to ME. 

A good attempt at fostering community comes in the form of challenges, however I find them to be quite hard to follow due to their lackluster appearance. Like seriously, read 30min per day? Instead of some sort of buildup? Or maybe even group challenges competing against one other to not only have a community, but a competitive edge?

All these ideas including the features, the adaptability of the app and making a proactive community are a great start. Just really want this app to flourish and become the thing I expect it to be in the process of living out my life to my fullest potential. If you’re reading this, Thanks for reading this far and I hope you have a blessed life!🙌

Absolutely good implementation of to-dos! Love it! Pets: I didn’t get why you need them in the game and what’s the mechanic behind them? Will they die if not fed? title: The best anti-procrastinating app
body:
The app works as a portal to a world called Habitica in which you create a character that levels up while you do tasks, to-dos and habits. In return, all mentioned before help you complete search and fighting quests from which you receive various rewards (exp., gold, eggs, equipment, etc.). The more you use it, the more you get. 

From my point of view, this is the best app I have ever used to push you to do your dailies, to dos and habits, all in one place. If you are in a party with at least one other enthusiast, you do a lot of real time activity/tasks in order to gain levels, coins and rewards! I recommend this to anyone who loves to play games, procrastinates but wants to quit and anyone that loves a challenge. 

The only things I really miss (since the new update really changed the app in a good way) is the option to buy the diamonds with coins (for subscribers) in the app, damage dealt to the boss under boss’ life left and when I click to-dos I lose life if there are many done at once. 

Thank you Habitica team for this app!

title: Pay to win
body:
It’s a great app and I definitely recommend it to anyone who is motivated by gamification. It’s a little confusing to navigate at first, but great once you get the hang of it. However if you want to collect all the pets and such, you have no choice but to subscribe. Pet quests can be gained if you join a party with people who have subscriptions, but for pets that can’t be obtained through quests you’re basically screwed. Challenges can give you gem rewards, but chances of winning are very slim. I would love if gems were purchasable with coins but were very expensive per gem to encourage people to either grind for them or subscribe. 
That being said I can see how that could be abused with FCV and spamming habits, so if that were implemented those things would need to be adjusted and capped. But I do think it’s doable and less scammy, and honestly a more motivating option. I’ve fallen off Habitica a lot because when those things are unattainable there’s little incentive to actually use the app
TL;DR: Good app overall but in my opinion the motivating factors are not sustainable. Claims not to be a pay to win game but absolutely is one if you want to collect things, which is the main reward system of the game. Needs adjustments

title: Used for a Full Year
body:
This is hands-down the best goal app I’ve ever used. All the game stuff aside, the goal functions are entirely customizable and easy to use. Organization is clean. The hardest time of this last year was when I stopped using it for a few months, and I’ve recently started using it again religiously; I’m never going back. 

The game aspect is fun. It’s pretty sweet hitting goals and then seeing my dude in full moon-armor riding a purple dragon with a banner and a sword. Really though it’s just an incredibly solid goal app with a couple fun twists. 

My ONLY critique; I wish the quests weren’t so hard to do solo. I’m not exactly super social, and I’d love to fight monsters by myself. I’ve been on the same lunar quest for a few months now.

Get this app and DIVE into it. My life would be nowhere near as organized without it, and you can tell someone put their heart and soul into designing it.

title: Good For Helping Me Improve, But Very Buggy!
body:
I have been using the app for nearly two years, and I have been able to steadily increase the number of tasks and frequency at which I do them. In that respect, I find the app very helpful for my ADHD.

However the app is extremely buggy. At least once a week, the app will tell me it started a new day, but it hasn’t cleared out my dailies from the previous day. I then can’t log my tasks for the current day until something about the server resets and finally refreshes so I can log my tasks.

Also, regardless of all the other improvements that have been made in the app, a glaring issue is that pressing the “+” button beside a task will not add the point to the task I selected, but to a completely different task. The haptic tracking is very off. It’s extremely frustrating that I have to tap the “+” to add points every time, I can’t just type it in. When my method of using the app is assigning points based on how hard the task is for me on a given day (sometimes my chronic pain conditions make a task much more difficult than on a different day), I have to repeatedly tap the “+” button to add those points that day. Sometimes I give myself 100 points for cleaning the toilet or doing the dishes, and having to press the button 100 times is so aggravating when the number glitches and adds some of the points elsewhere instead.

Can this be addressed in an upcoming update, please? The haptic feedback badly needs adjusting. Some days these bugs are so bad, I don’t even want to use the app at all.

author: SunflowerValentine

title: Moving in the WRONG direction!!!!
body:
⭐☆☆☆☆

I realize I’m late to this news, but I just rediscovered Habitica after using it consistently from 2020 through 2023 — and I genuinely cannot believe the guilds are gone.

The guilds were the soul of this app. That’s not dramatic — that’s accurate. They were how I found goal-specific communities, niche challenges, accountability partners, and like-minded people pushing toward the same achievements. Whether it was fitness, language learning, productivity sprints, or life resets, guilds created momentum. They made change feel communal instead of lonely.

Coming back, I was actually excited. I thought, “Okay, let’s see what guilds are active now. Let’s plug back in.” And they just… don’t exist. That completely deflates the experience. The app without guilds feels like a stripped-down habit tracker with RPG cosmetics. Functional? Sure. Inspiring? Not even close.

What makes this more frustrating is the subscription fee. You’re charging $4.99/month. If moderation was the issue, raise the price. Gate guild access behind subscription. Recruit paid moderators. Build a scaled-down version. There were options. Eliminating them entirely feels like removing the engine because maintaining it was inconvenient.

I understand this happened a while ago. I’m just rediscovering the app now, and the downgrade hits hard. The excitement, the optimism, the sense of shared transformation — gone. For an app built around gamified self-improvement, removing the primary social motivation system feels like a massive strategic misstep.

Really disappointing.

title: Helpful, but actual fun content is hidden behind a paywall
body:
Habitica has 2 currencies: gems and coins. Coins you can get for free by doing tasks but gems are mostly given via the monthly subscription, they CAN be gotten for free however it’s insanely tedious

Gems are basically where all the actually fun stuff for the game is hidden. The quests and many customization items are stuck behind gem paywalls, so without them or a person in your party thst has premium and can buy the party quests, the game is just boring grinding with basically no real end goal

The way to get gems for free is also flawed, the only ways are website giveaways or challenges, which will give you tasks and is basically gambling. You join challenges, complete tasks, and have a random chance of getting selected to win gems. This however completely ruins the betterment aspect of the game as since it’s literally just gambling, you’re pushed to join as many challenges as you can physically handle, and to actually have a good chance at getting gems, you have to just lie and say you did it. It’s the only real way to get any. Plus, completing challenges gives you in game coins, which when you’re forced to lie about it basically just gives you free money and ruins any actual habit building.

In all, fine game, bad way of dealing with the ptw currency. Personally, I believe small amounts of gems should be given to you if you go on habitica daily, like 1 per month, and the longer your streak gets, the more gems you’re given. It’d still make gems annoying to get for free players (2 months for a single hair color) and keep players keeping up their habits naturally while still being able to do fun activities like quests.

title: Pomodoro Timer (HabiFocus) request
body:
Dear Habitica Team,

I’m writing to submit a feature request for a built-in Habitica-themed Pomodoro timer (HabiFocus)—a tool that would gamify focus sessions and tie directly into Habitica’s core RPG/task system, boosting productivity for the community while staying true to the app’s fun, quest-based vibe.

Core Concept for HabiFocus

The timer would align with the classic Pomodoro method and integrate seamlessly with Habitica’s existing rewards/mechanics:

• A 25-minute HabiFocus work session = earn a small Gold reward

• A 5-minute HabiRest break 

• 4 completed HabiFocus cycles = a HabiVictory long break, plus a random Loot drop (e.g., potions, eggs) as a bonus reward

Why This Matters for Habitica

This feature would bridge the gap between focus and task completion—something many users already try to do with third-party Pomodoro tools—by making productivity a native part of the Habitica experience. It would enhance the app’s core value of turning daily habits into a fun quest, and appeal to students, remote workers, and anyone using Habitica to build consistent focus routines.

I think this timer would be a fantastic addition to Habitica’s existing features, and I’d love to see how the team could refine the mechanics to fit the app’s world. Please let me know if you need any additional details or feedback from the community to develop this idea further!

Thank you for all the hard work you put into making Habitica such a wonderful, motivating tool for building better habits. I’m excited to see the app grow and evolve.

title: The idea has limitless potential but the execution is awful
body: There's so many ways that this idea could be good, but clearly the devs just stopped at "good enough." I just want an app that makes creating a routine fun, and I love rpg's so I figured this would be a real winner. I'm assuming the dev is like 50+ years old and never actually played a real rpg video game from this era. My guess is that they spend  99% of their time playing D&D, because all rpg elements are clearly inspired by it. It'd also explain the choice of 1980's graphics. When I finally got to go on my first quest, I thought "finally, something to do other than collecting useless items" but I was quickly back to being disappointed. Like D&D, you have to imagine going on a quest. Why there's not actually any real monsters to fight with your character is beyond me. There's also absolutely no purpose in any of the classes. Nothing changes from being a rogue or a mage, the entire class system is arbitrary. It's basically this: want more useless items, pick a rogue, want more useless experience points, pick a mage, etc. The only thing that resembles anything like a video game rpg is the HP and damage system. Don't do a task on your list, take damage. Ultimately, I'm deciding to uninstall this app because there's no way to interact with it on the apple watch. The habit/task tracking is good, I'm just not interested in collecting useless junk and pointless pets that do nothing. So, I might as well just switch to a normal tracker that has some apple watch capabilities.

title: Love this app!
body:
My friends and I use this to stay motivated and keep each other accountable. I know it’s just an RPG that can easily be cheated, but somehow we don’t want to cheat and the game keeps us engaged. Just bought an annual subscription which I rarely do for apps.

Easily 5/5 stars from me because of how effective it has been for me, but to be honest and transparent I think this app should get 4/5 stars because of a severe limitation: lack of an offline mode and robust syncing. I know it’s a hard problem but Dropbox figured out syncing almost 20 years ago, and rival task management app Things has had robust cloud (and local!) syncing for many years now.

Other things I’d like to see:
-More task management features. To Do’s seems to be the weakest of the three main lists. You can do almost anything with combinations of hashtags and filtering but it’s clumsy. I use only Habitica for habit/daily tracking, but I use Things for task management and move To Do’s from Things to Habitica when I want to prioritize them (or get XP for them, ha).
- Variety in quest mechanics. Yes, quests have different pixel art and descriptions, but they are all essentially the same, either boss battles or collection quests that are just a matter of racking up hits on the boss or collecting items. Why not combine them with specific tasks (like Challenges?) so there is some variety?
- More content to keep the engagement going. I felt a sense of completeness after completing the “final” quest (Lost Masterclasser) and dropped off the app for a bit. I think more community engagement could keep the app evergreen. In addition to letting people make Challenges, why not bring back incentives for people to write quest lines etc.? Reading the wiki it looks like people used to be able to get awards for contributing in various ways beyond submitting code.

Thanks again for the amazing app, really appreciate the work you are all doing!

title: I keep trying to like it
body:
But honestly it makes no sense. 

It’s not intuitive. I’m not motivated to do more because it’s not clear what the goal is or how I gain anything. Currency, mounts, clothing items, etc all seem to be random on what they require or how to obtain them. I honestly thought this entire game was microtransactions until I got into a menu where I in fact did have currency. I’m still not clear how items work or what to do with them though.

It says I get certain items for events on my notification but it’s not clear how to obtain them or if you’ve obtained them to equip them? It’s not clear how I can use anything this app offers as far as “rewards” to motivate myself at all. I use it as a checklist and that’s it. I set all my habits to monthly so I can see what I’ve done this month but it’s ridiculous when it resets on the first and there’s no way to view your history of chores. You lose a level if you run out of life. The app doesn’t care if you’re sick and has no option to really skip a day if you have another person to pickup dailies for you.

This app does nothing for me motivation wise and as much as I wanted it to work for my life it just doesn’t. Sunk cost fallacy is the only reason I’ve kept it this long. Devs barely tried and provide 0 instruction or direction to the player on how to even use the thing, much less how to customize anything or actually use it as a tool. Completing tasks does nothing, same with not completing them because the game doesn’t give you anything to look forward to or work towards. It’s really not clear what the goal of the game is and I’m not going to keep trying to figure it out.

title: They downgraded it
body:
Been meaning to review for a while. At first, I loved this app— it helped me a lot in college. But they removed the Guild feature, which probably wouldn’t be such a big deal if the guild I was in hadn’t been one of the most helpful aspects for me. I have ADHD, and I was in a guild that basically acted as a sort of support group where we could exchange tips or just share stories. Lots of us tried to message the dev team about how detrimental losing our guild would be, but every message was met with the same generic “we appreciate your feedback” corporate response. 
Granted, Habitica “relocated” the guild chats to Discord, so we can still communicate, but that meant having to go to a completely different platform to do so instead of having it in the same location as the other features, which is a huge mental roadblock for ADHDers like me. This led to me losing a lot of my motivation to use the app, and I’ve barely touched it since.

title: Love it!
body:
I’ve been using Habitica for a few weeks now, and I absolutely adore it. I have ADHD and really struggle to form good habits and stay on task. I love that I can break up tasks into smaller bits to check off, that’s huge for me. And having the dailies to be accountable to is so helpful, this has genuinely been the best I’ve taken care of my teeth in my whole life (I really struggle to floss especially).

The only request I could think of would be to be able to see how equipment looks on my avatar before I buy it, because sometimes I don’t like the way it looks! This is a very minor problem though because you can have things equipped (& get the benefits) without them appearing on your avatar. Also, are you able to gift equipment? It would be nice to have the option to send to friends.

Truly, I just really love this app and hope I continue to use it for a long time!

title: Needs modern features
body: It’s an incredible app suffering from a lack of meaningful development. Some bug fixes here, new cosmetics there, but very little work done on actual new features, especially to take advantage of modern iOS. For instance, let me integrate metrics like steps. Why does the widget barely update, and why can I not check off habits from the widget? Where is the watchOS app? On and on. I’d happily pay the subscription fee but the app barely feels like it’s in active development so I don’t know what I’d be paying for. What is the roadmap here?

title: I love this app!! 💜
body:
I don’t understand why Habitica is only 4 stars right now, it’s amazing?!?!? I mean, it has a few bugs but they do not bother me much, if at all.
I have been using Habitica for a year and a half now and I have stuck to it more than any other habit/productivity app. It is far more customizable than any other similar app I have used. You can create habits, dailies, and to-do tasks, and tweak all of them to fit your routine best. Plus it’s all gamified! SUPER helpful for someone with ADHD. 
There is an optional subscription, but it is really not needed at all to get the most out of the app. Every feature is free, the subscription just lets you in on some fun extras. But the base app is wonderful on its own! 

I HIGHLY recommend you to try this app because it’s completely free with no ads or anything and the subscription feels very optional and not pushy at all. Especially if you have ADHD, have trouble keeping track of your tasks, or want extra motivation for doing them, this is the right app for you.

title: Joyful Habit-Building Tool
body: This app has been my little source of happiness over the past few days. I love its clean and thoughtful design, with sections for Habits, Routines, and To-Dos, and the satisfying color changes for tasks. The ability to set personalized ‘rewards’ is a great touch, and the party feature adds a supportive, community-driven aspect that I really appreciate. The progress visualization is motivating, and the gamification elements are minimal—just the right amount for me. Overall, it’s a delightful, lightweight tool that brings joy and a sense of support, making it perfect for habit building and daily task management. Thank you to the developers for creating something so lovely!☺️

title: Works but the bullies aren’t worth it
body:
I really liked this app. I’ve enjoyed it and it helps. However, the players can be very toxic when it comes to parties. Recently I was bullied out of a party for not wanting to join a challenge due to my mental health. I can’t believe the things people will say to you in an app about self improvement (kys). title: ABSOLUTELY Awesome App!
body:
This app is Absolutely Awesome, If you stick with it long enough to figure out how it should work. It takes a bit time to get use to and figure out the point system according to your personal tasks, especially trying to figure out how to write dailies that won’t cause you to die to quick or barely do damage.
After using this app EVERY single day for 5 months and actually getting things done in my life for it, my only 2 asks would be for the ability to create folders that can hold ones tasks and the folders can be expanded instead of having to use tags and constantly have to click on and off to find and isolate my different tasks. Ive gotten really good at using the tags but folders would be 100x easier on my eyes and on my mind.
My second ask would be to have the ability gain points for each subtask that is completed under a task, as well as different difficulties for subtasks, and the ability to make certain subtasks required and others optional, because subtasks feel like something I use so often but are just completely useless in the way that they currently appear.

Ill end this with a few of my favorite features.
The ability to make my allocated points be distributed depending on the task that was completed is absolutely genius, and I love the fact that parties can do quests together, I only with the boss damages where shared between bosses.

My last piece of input is that I have contemplating many times in paying $9 of a party with the extra $3, but for some reason I only see that this offer is available on desktop and not mobile. I only wish there was maybe a video or something that could inform me on exactly what the offer contains and how it visually looks on desktop ASWELL as Mobile.

Over all, My Favorite app in the app store and I can’t see myself ever letting it go with how much more productive I've become.

title: Literally Changing my Life
body:
TL:DR: App is literally changing my life at work and in my personal life. It uses social features and really simple design mechanics (sound, color, etc) to help you complete stuff. Highly recommended if you don’t mind the paywall. 

I want to say a big thank you to Habitica for making this app, because it’s actively changing my day-to-day life. I had been really struggling in almost every aspect of my life—especially work—to get done what I needed to get done. This simple app has helped me get more done in a few weeks than I have in months, and it’s genuinely helped me so much. If I can’t get motivated to do a task, I will put it in Habitica, and that alone will help me get it done. 

Some things I didn’t know when I downloaded that I think would have tipped me over sooner:
•You have habits, “dailies,” and to-dos. Your habits will change colors based on whether or not you do them *or* mark that you didn’t do them. This color changing alone has me 10x more likely to do a habit lol
•Your to-dos change color based on how long they’ve sat in your to-do list. They turn bright red when they’re not done
•You can weight the difficulty of a task

I find the “getting stuff” aspect of the app less appealing, so the paywall doesn’t bug me much, though if your main motivation would be getting pets/weapons/etc, I can see how it could be troublesome. The simple color-chancing mechanic of all the sections is really effective for me.

The guild feature is SUPER motivating, as well. I love joining in on quests with my guild. I just got a group of friends to join so that we could make a guild together! 

Love the app. God bless you guys!

The Pros? It’s free.

This app, this game, gave me real-time rewards for doing the mundane, rather than having to wait and see if or when my wife would thank me for doing the dishes or taking out the trash as needed. I had habits that I wanted to break (such as setting repeat alarms or getting back into bed after turning off my alarm and potentially falling back asleep). author: KDANETH

body:
I am a data scientist in my 30s and I absolutely love Habitica and use it with my partner. We both have elaborate wardrobes and can be found hollering across the house to come look at eachother's Habitica outfit despite having used it for like 4 years now. There are pay-to-play features but they are not absolute (there are other ways to access those items through the MMO community interaction aspect, it's just harder and less likely) and the basal experience is good enough. I didn't pay for I think the first year; it's $5/mo if you want a consistent in-game monthly income of the higher-tier in-game currency, basically. 

To summarize, you have your own content you can interact with, and other people out in the external Habitica world (you don't walk around on a map, you join groups and essentially engage in an automated tabletop RPG by completing your task list with the computer as the DM). It is 4-seasonal with 4 themed events where you can acquire items that may or may not recur. There is a huge, huge variety of pets you can hatch and evolve (one stage evolution) in any potion color (there are I think 7 basic and an unknown amt of special potions). This is my favorite part. 

The community is very active in improving the codebase and you can create and contribute objects yourself as a pixel artist, though not 100% of submissions are used / you have to get on github and get picked to make them (but it's achievable); there are in-game awards for this kind of contribution. 

I use it for managing my basic self-care tasks and simple errands as I have a chronic illness. Before I was a data scientist I also used it to motivate myself to study coding. There are both boolean valued (check-off) tasks and activities that you can claim an unlimited # of rewards for; you create them. You control this size of the reward you get for the tasks and there is a workaround system to adjust your settings (your gold and mana) if you mess something up or there's a glitch (I've never used this). You cannot alter your amount of the higher-tier currency, potions, etc. and must get a mod to help you if you experience a glitch there (this has happened to me one time, and it was because my internet was flickering in and out rapidly right at the very moment that the reward for the group tabletop-style quest was marked complete; I had other glitches in other softwares due to my computer's behavior so it wasn't their fault but they fixed it within 24hrs). 

Everyone is there in good faith. There are identity-based and task-based groups and a server-wide groupchat for interacting with mods on various pragmatic issues like previously discussed. I forget how, but I don't think Habitica hires mods, I think people become mods through a certain amount of community contribution (might be wrong on this); also anyone can start a group if you have a small amount of the higher-tier currency to put in your group's bank (but you can pull it right back out afterwards, heh). There is a group that goes around taking over and "robbing" the banks of abandoned groups and it has become Habitica-sanctioned, which I love.

Okay, this description is getting out of control. There's a ton more. It's really good. However the gameplay is NOT so spin-offy that it becomes a timewaster in and of itself; doing your tasks drives everything.

title: Helpful beyond belief, and such a wholesome environment!
body:
This app (and website) are exactly what I needed in my life. I joined about five or six months ago now, and Habitica has really helped me get my life together. I have ADHD and severe anxiety, and keeping track of what I need to do (not to mention doing it) has always been a challenge for me.

Before, I’d just make checklists on my computer or scraps of paper each day, but it was annoying having to essentially re-do the list every day (either re-writing it or unchecking the checked stuff that needed to be done daily), plus it was really easy to forget things that needed to be added to the list.

With Habitica, I can easily keep track of all my daily tasks, and even tasks that repeat but not as frequently. I can make tasks repeat every x months, weeks, or days, or even have things repeat on specific days (every M/W/F, for example). Repeating tasks and one-time tasks are kept separate, and I can add due dates for the one-time tasks. Tags make it easy to sort tasks/habits, and if I ever want to rearrange where things fall on my list, that’s a breeze too!

Fun quests and rewards make it easy to keep me going, especially with my habits. I’m very rewards-oriented, and there have been multiple occasions where I haven’t wanted to work on my habits but was motivated into it because I wanted to do more damage to the boss I was fighting. I was worried that I’d obtain everything possible pretty soon and then lose my motivation, but there’s so much to do and more comes along all the time!

Everyone on the site is so welcoming and supportive; it’s a very wholesome environment. I was scared to ask questions at first, in case people were mean about me not knowing/understanding things, but every time I have asked a question or read the Tavern chat logs, everyone has been kind, helpful, and supportive in everything they say.

There are things you can pay real money for, but everything is fairly priced and you can also access 99% of things without paying real money anyway. The only things you can’t get without paying real money are subscriber-exclusive items, which come out monthly but are really only cosmetic; they offer no in-game benefits other than looking neat. And there’s definitely plenty of neat-looking stuff without that, too!

Habitica has changed my life, and I am so, so grateful for all that it provides—to me, and to everyone else who finds it helpful in their lives.

Good luck, everyone! Whatever it is you want to be changing in your life, I know you can do it :)

body: I loved this app for a while, it gives you rewards for doing every day things and makes you feel like you’ve accomplished something. But then the gems. Gems are the in game currency you have to purchase with real money (different to gold which you can earn). Having to buy game currency is one of my biggest pet peeves. You can’t convert gold to gems, you can’t sell stuff to get gems, and it’s nearly impossible to get them. The only way to get them is to do “challenges” posted by other users which are difficult to do for 1-2 gems (which is not guaranteed. Some challenges only 1 person wins). Another way is to “contribute” which I have yet to figure out what that means but from the tings I have seen it is minimal pay out as well. I wanted to get all of the pets and unlocked all of the ones you can get through day to say activity, but “quests” take forever and rarely give you eggs to hatch so I have not gotten many of those either. The only way to get new potions (after the core 11) is to buy them with gems. Basically, don’t get this app if you actually want to unlock everything or complete quests and missions. I’ve had this app for over a year and I’m considering deleting because I’ve exhausted everything I can do

Habitica has been great at updating the app and it’s already loads better, but just be warned if you are downloading the app for the first time, it’s not perfect yet.

For instance: my laptop was stolen and I am changing all my passwords. I can’t do that in the app. Seems a little unsafe and quite a flaw. 

I’d love to report this in the app itself, but I don’t have email set up on my phone, so I can’t. (For the record, yes, this is an old-person problem, but I don’t want constant emails on my phone, okay? Why can’t you just give me the email address?)

Once again, Habitica is a great place and so worth your time. Just maybe don’t spend all your time on the app just yet.

title: Top notch, would recommend
body:
I started using this app after reading a glowing recommendation on a ‘how to get things done’ site, and it has not disappointed. Much like the grownup version of a sticker chart, this app encourages the user to perform those boring day to day chores and tasks that we keep meaning to do but forget about. Some particular things I like:

- the fact that before rolling over to the next day, it will ask you what things you may have forgotten to check off the day before, so you don’t get penalized for ‘not logging in’

-the variety of categories tasks can be put in: one time items vs once a day items vs multiple times a day items

-being able to subdivide tasks into smaller sub take by using checklists

Some things I’d really like to see:

-the ability to send other members in your party a task—I feel like this would be especially useful for shopping lists

-being able to save or repost a past to-do. This would be great for those chores that are infrequent or dependent on some sort of irregular outside thing (the weather) but involve enough complexity that recreating could be a pain. To limit lag and storage this could be limited to saving up to 5 to-dos?

That said, all of this would be bonus material and I intend to keep using this app long term and recommending it to others.

title: Habitica can be a total Game Changer
body:
I’ve been using Habitica for almost two years now, and I’m here to say that as I was initially a casual  user of the app, and have moved to being a player in a world parallel yet decidedly different from our own. With Habitica being a highly customizable game, you truly can gamify your habits and tasks to suit your own level of creativity, utilitarianism, minimalism, and community engagement. The guilds are supportive and members are eager to give encouragement and feedback, and the challenges that the guilds provide are usually well written and sometimes use “RPG lingo” to make it more like a game and less like a chore list. 
I started changing the names of my tasks to “unlock achievements “ and my habit lists to “Activate power ups “ , and it’s been significantly helpful to keep my attention and engagement with the app. Furthermore: purchasing the app is going to be the game changer. While you don’t technically “need” to, it opens up another level of interest and engagement with special Pet and potion Quests, and Habitica gives you a bundle of items every month you subscribe, and a special little pet as a thank you. Purchases keep the app free and free of ads for free users. 

However, this month I found that the Mystery Gift items did not show up in my Items list. I’m wondering if it’s a bug

title: Inclusive phobia protection feature!!!
body:
I use the app with a few friends and it’s great for keeping track of habits and giving me external motivation - which I definitely need to make new habits/ keep up tough ones. 

I’m really excited about the phobia protection feature though. It is an add-on that will remove images of spiders, snakes, zombies, etc - things people may have phobias of. One of the friends that uses Habitica with me has a massive phobia of spiders and, while I think she’s ok with digital spiders, I never realized how apps I use easily (and invited her to use with me) might not be accessible to her during Halloween. I didn’t realize how important this kind of feature is for inclusivity until I saw it. I know how stressful the phobia is for her in person and I appreciate that Habitica is providing an option for people to avoid seeing potentially upsetting images when they’re everywhere during Halloween season. 

I just had to drop a review because this kind of feature makes apps accessible to everyone- as they should be. It shows me that Habitica has people behind it that care about other people.
author: jnpwebb

title: Gamification done RIGHT.
body:
So many productivity gurus will tell you to “gamify” things in your life to get things done. It’ll help you stop procrastinating they say!

But if you ASK what they mean by that, you get vague terms like “reward systems” and “set it like an appointment so you don’t miss it”

You know what reward system WORKS? A HEALTH BAR AND A SKILL TREE

You know what “appointment” I never miss? My daily tasks on animal crossing and that sweet, sweet LoL match with my friends. 

Habitica brings the gaming experience to mundane tasks. 
Did you take out your trash today? XP!
Did you fold the laundry even though you hate it and would rather pull out you own eyeballs? MOAR XP!
Did you make that appointment with your doc that you’ve been putting off for 6 months +?! XP GALORE!

Join a guild or set up a party with friends! Get REALLY competitive with you avatar looks. It’s all in the name of XP... I mean... ADULTIN... I mean... PRODUCTIVITY!

title: Great app, but could be even better

There are some small improvements I would LOVE to see from the game that would really add to it!

1. You can score the difficulty of the tasks you would like to accomplish, which give rewards proportionate to the difficulty. I find that this game works the best when I set the difficulty to hard, as that’s the only real way that I feel truly accomplished and rewarded for doing things. I think the rewards should be even better.

2. Leveling up doesn’t really do much. You have to get all the way to level 10 to even choose a class. I need something to incentivize me to really really wanna level up.

3. I wish there was an actual game I could play with my character, like a JRPG style turn-based combat system. Your character DOES fight bosses, but you don’t really get to join them.

This game is really on it’s way to something great, but I’m really hoping for a big overhaul of content soon!!

title: Really Helpful for School!
body:
It’s ridiculously hard to stay motivated during virtual classes, and I think Habitica has been a big help! I have all my school assignments up on my To-Do list, which is really helpful for keeping track of what to do and for staying motivated in the middle of working on an assignment.

The main reason why I love it so much is that it’s ridiculously effective for me and it’s just what I was looking for. A lot of other habit-tracker/to-do list apps aren’t in an engaging format, and I delete them after slowly losing interest over the course of a few days. I didn’t have this problem with Habitica, because of how it’s part game and part productivity tracker. I’ve been looking for an app like this for ages, and I didn’t find this until my friend recommended it (and thank goodness she did).

I haven’t noticed any bugs, other than the occasional small bug that comes from not syncing with the happening on my computer quickly enough. Occasionally there’s an issue where I check off a To-Do list item or a Daily and it doesn’t change color immediately, but it’s no big deal because the color changes if I go to another tab and then go back to the original. I’m also not entirely sold on the idea of gems basically being only obtainable through money, but I can appreciate that the things they purchase confer mostly cosmetic benefit.

title: Can't imagine a world without it
body:
I've been using Habitica for years. And, let me tell you: as someone with ADHD, this single fact is actually much more significant than it sounds. 

I have struggled all my life to find an app (or series of apps and schedules and reminders and calendars and motivation to *just keep trying hard enough*) to keep my days together. Nothing has ever stuck aside from Habitica. I absolutely loved and still love the Moleskine suite of apps, but my chaotic, unfocused, and tired brain just can't do minimalism successfully. 

Habitica, on the other hand, is enormously flexible and expansive, perhaps even overwhelmingly so at first. That said, there is a large & active community of users available to give you ideas for how to use the app and also to encourage you along the way. The community truly puts other apps that boast a "social" component to shame.  

For me personally, I do use the app to work on habits I'm trying to develop, but I also use it for pretty much every other logistical aspect of my life: project management, collecting/bookmarking, reminders, delegation, and brainstorming. I would be an absolute mess without it.

So if you have ADHD or you struggle to keep everything together, I cannot recommend this app enough. Give it a try.
