It’s fun, it’s simple, and it’s effective. I’m so happy there is a team that created this idea and put it into the world, this is exactly what I needed. I’ve been using it for close to a year now. When I’m having some depressive episodes, I’m able to pause the “game” until I’m confident in my ability to get back on my feet. Which is something I’m /so/ thankful for. No, I’m not a bot, and I have not been paid a single penny to say any of this. I just genuinely love this app so much. I wanted to show my gratitude towards the developers and everyone that participates in the making and improvement of this app, because it changed my life and I’m forever grateful.

-Be able to choose what days you do your dailies on. For example, instead of choosing daily for my schoolwork, I can checkmark Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, and leave Sunday and Saturday unchecked, as I don’t do school on those days.

-A priority system that prevents spending coins until the user completed the prioritized task. Example: I set school as a priority that prevents me from spending coins on rewards if I don’t have that priority checked off for the day. It’s possible to make lots of money off of less important dailies, habits, or to dos and reward yourself without doing the other, more important and/or more challenging tasks. 

Otherwise, such a great app that really helps hold me accountable to the goals I want to achieve in a fun way!

title: Keep on track
body:
With the quarantine, me and my friends felt like time was fake, cause it is. My one friend found this and we all downloaded it. It helps us remember to finish all our tasks, and remember to do our simple ones. It’s easy to use, and makes us excited to find things to do. Its helping us actually get around to stuff during a really weird time. 

It’s basically a Dnd to-do list, but it’s really fun. The quests especially make me want to do the tasks. 

Now for some negatives, it’s an honor code. Technically nothing is stopping you from just checking stuff off, but that’s just a general negative with every to do list. The app is a little tricky to customize the character, specifically weapons and equipment. It’s a little out of the way, and you have to know where to look a little bit. The app is also a little slow to load, but if you leave the page and go back to your to-dos or your habits, it usually straightens itself out. 

I highly recommend this, it’s really motivating, and doesn’t take that much effort to set up!

Got a birthday you need to remember to get gift and mail off by a certain day? Put it on to-do with checklist of “buy gift” and “mail gift” to make sure you don’t forget!

Wanna break a habit? Chewing nails or not drinking enough water? Add it to habits and get rewarded for each bottle you drink or lose some HP when you catch yourself chewing nails.

These are just some examples from personal experience. I’ve been using this app almost a full year now and it continues to help me while being amusing as my work pays off in striking down my foes and gaining cute pets along the way.

Would highly recommend, especially if you’re like me and suffer from mental troubles or needing a pay off to aide your motivation to improve life.

title: THIS GOT MY LIFE TOGETHER
body:
I literally love everything about this app. It got my entire life together. I credit it for my productivity in every aspect. It really is perfectly tailored for the user. A couple reasons why you should totally get this app:

-The combination of ways to write tasks is soooo convenient! There are dailies for what you do on a repeated day to day or week to week basis, habits for things you want to do but aren’t quite doing every day yet, and a to-do list. This way I can keep “brush your teeth”, “keep your room clean”’ and “organize your desk” separated by appropriate category.

-The gaming aspect is AWESOME! With other apps you check something off your todo and then that’s it. No real reward. With Habitica I get excited to level up or buy new items for my avatar! Plus I can make my own rewards so I can buy myself set rewards like “go out for ice cream” with currency I earn by completing my tasks.

-With every missed daily or negative habit you lose life. This keeps me motivated to stay on top of things. But if I do fall behind, I just have to work a bit harder to buy a healing potion that can bring my health back up. I have to use the same gold that would be going towards my rewards otherwise, so it’s good motivation to stay productive.

Honestly, just give this app a try. It’s really worth it. If you’re the type to be motivated by games, leveling up, and earning rewards, this is definitely the best app you can have for this type of thing.

author: smoochking

title: Absolutely Amazing! Except....
body:
I love this app. Having that little ding sound whenever I complete a task is incredible. It makes me want to do my things so bad because it puts stake in it.

It’s fun, and relaxed, and all the guilds I’m in are so supportive! I’ve started doing things that I previously did once or twice a week every single day. I’m legitimately excited about completing my tasks!

The RPG style makes the whole thing a game, and if you love farming games like me (any Slime Rancher bois in the house?), it’s absolutely perfect because you’ve already got the app structure wired into your brain. It really works.

I appreciate the lower pressure option of habits versus dailies, which lets me separate out the needs and the wants. Make sure you don’t overstock your dailies!! Be realistic, love yourself, and remember: if you set the goal to high, you’ll come to resent the goal and quite possibly resent the whole app system that is otherwise so helpful. Be realistic. It’s ok if you can’t do everything. Baby steps!

Also, put everything in there. Even the little things. It makes such a huge difference to have every little thing that is a chore or needs to be a habit get positive reinforcement, because it makes me so much more excited to complete the harder tasks!

Now for the Except... 

My only problem? The sound when you click the plus for a habit.... it’s low, and honestly sounds like a failure sound. I hate it, and it makes me unhappy because my gamer brain doesn’t feel like I accomplished something, it feels like I lost a life or took a hit. It’s a low sound, and I turn off the sound every time I click plus on a habit because I can’t stand it and it makes me sad. It’s such a shame because the other sounds for success are so happy!!! Please, please change it. I did something. Good, and that sound makes me want to cry because it sounds like I failed.

I’m sorry, I know this seems like an overreaction, I just... it really makes a difference for me. 

Outside of that, this app is wonderful and I really appreciate it.

If it was forum based (like a subreddit) people could look up keywords for the exact topics or posts they could converse in

Cheers!

title: Wonderful App!
body:
I love Habitica! I have used this service off and on since it was created, but recently I have started using Habitica every day. I love the separation between Habits, To Dos, and Dailies, as well as the gentle character customization and the inclusion of a place to converse with other players. 

I have encountered bugs where my items will not be checked off until I do it a few times, or the app will lag when putting a new item. That is the reason for my Four Stars instead of Five. Also, I would really like if we could tag each task under a category, and be able to track that tag with the tasks we did. I think it would be nice to see how many times I checked “Clean my room” and not just as part of a streak. 

Overall, this app is a great way to keep track of your to-dos. Its interface is simple but effective, and works well for people who enjoy a bit of fun even among the mundane. This is not a full “game,” for anyone confused, but adds an entertainment factor, as well as a rewarding one, for those looking to be more productive. I have tried many productivity apps, and this is the one I consistently remember and come back to. Thank you for making this app!

title: For those of us who need a little extra nudge of motivation.
body:
This game is it. It’s adorable and easy to use. So your chores or projects or just daily habits you want to make routine are rewarded instantly. (You know us millennials with our instant gratification)
You might one day go for a run and pick up an egg! Panda, wolf, dragon? You may stumble upon a quest to complete with your friends, or you can just hack away at your own habits; either way it’s a great idea. 
This app has helped me immensely. I’ve always wanted to have a routine because humans are generally happier when they follow one. I just couldn’t force myself to do things like get out of bed before 9 or brushing my hair or doing my school work. 
I have moderate to severe depression which makes day to day habits that most people do without thinking a lot more difficult for me. Even things like just driving to the pharmacy to get my anti depressants. So if I find something difficult, I put it in my habitica list and it gives me an extra nudge of motivation. 
Five stars for sure.

body:
This app is everything I’ve been dreaming of. I used a Striiv as a teen and loved the garden game and being able to turn my physical activity into a video game. This app offer similar potential but needs some major work before its fully functional. 

1. I can’t scroll down in the challenges tab. I have a new iPad Pro and have yet to try on my iPhone. It’s frustrating i can only see the first few challenges, and when i scroll down as soon as my finger releases the screen shoots back to the top. Fix please. 

2. (Please don’t take this the wrong way bc i identify as a nerd too) and something us nerds do is hella over complicate things. I think if the UI was simplified it would make way more sense. And, issues would be easier to mitigate. 

3. It would be SUPER COOL if you could work with Nerd Fitness and get a thing going. If you’ve never heard of it look it up. I really feel like there could be a ton of amazing things of you worked with them, especially since getting healthy is a big reason why i, and others, are interested in the app. 

4. As an artist i would cream my shorts if i could use my own fantasy art for my avatar. Actually, I’d be willing to pay money monthly just for this option. Especially if you’d let it change it an infinite amount of times (some apps don’t, weird) so i could ‘grow’ my character w me. 

5. I haven’t spent much time in this app so forgive me if this i already a thing.... but... i would love if we could set personal challenges that only we get to see, Nd every time we do something for that challenge we see it as a percentage. Just thinking about my goal tracker on my browser and how great that would be in this app. Ex- a goal of mine is to read 20 books this year. Every time i read one i see it as a percentage, and it just really helps me motivate myself. 

I’d love to change this to a 5 star.

title: Can you add (Goals)?
body:
Hello developers, I love this app though I wish I can add goals to my busy schedule. I think you should add another section similar to the others (habits, daily, to dos) and then right next to it “Goals”!   The goals should be able to be added anywhere and anytime. And the goals should be able to messed around with in the terms of the reward you get (coins and xp)  

For example,  I want to fix up my car and make it look nicer, and to do that I will need to do a lot of stuff such as: Oil change, New rims, new tires, clean the interior, wax my car, new steering wheel, work on the body, and just straight up detail my car.   I believe these fall under a different level of importance other than to do’s and habits. Mainly because I more than likely can’t get all those done in one day, and I feel I should be rewarded for those accomplishments...

For example,  “Oil Change” I rarely have enough time to get an oil change so I would put it in the “Goals” section and when I create that goal I will set the xp for 20 and gold for 100.   That way when I finally get around to it I will be rewarded for my sacrifice (Time and money).  

Not to mention making a “Goals” section would improve people’s motivation “ok oil change for 100 gold one step closer to getting a good weapon”. At least that’s how I feel. 

  Finally to the developers I took my time and patience from the day to write this to you so please respond or do something to let me know you saw my idea.  Also the app is amazing but I’m only putting four stars so you can see my review, thanks for your time

-Matthew Amperano

title: Habitica revolutionized the to-do app—now it needs to be one
body:
A thing I've learned about productivity apps—the less intuitively they fit your workflow, the more prone you are to fall off the wagon. I loved Habitica (then still HabitRPG) for it's brilliant (and charmingly nerdy) incentivization to stay on top of everything—and ultimately fell out of use because of a lack of a solid mobile UI (disincentivize).

Fortunately, it's come a long way, and with a much more intuitive interface on both desktop and mobile, it's a viable solution for everyone—not just those willing to make concessions for a killer concept.

The problem? Habitica's brilliant game-ified approach to the to-do list is hindered by its actual to-do list mechanics.

• A color-coded category system for home, work, etc (like is standard in most to-do apps)? Sorry, Habitica already uses colors for its "task value" mechanic. And no categories, just a rudimentary tag system. And sorting is manual only, (and because it needs to sync any single change you make before you can make another, it's an arduous process). Getting your tasks organized at a glance is not really an option.
• Push notification reminders for dailies/weeklies (Habitica's recurring routine tasks, which are separate from its one-time tasks)? They fire on seemingly random days, whether the task is due that day or not. Seems to be a bug some users have been suffering for months.
• Dailies that are due once every five days? You can do that, BUT: if it's the kind of task that, if you miss when it's due on Monday, needs to be done on Tuesday instead of waiting until Saturday, Habitica does not have you covered.
• Dailies that need to be done three times a week? Sorry, you have to specify which days of the week specifically.

Can they be worked around? Yeah, to some degree. But again: disincentives.

I understand the allure of Habitica is the game aspect, and as such, that's where most of the development resources go. But it's a little frustrating to see all the updates about special weapons and events when all the above issues persist, and start to have me keeping my actual tasks in 2Do (do you know how many dragons are in 2Do? ZERO).

title: This is what I was looking for!
body:

I realized I needed accountability and a rewards system, so I started my own on a wall calendar with tally marks...when lo and behold, my coworker alerted me to the existence of Habitica! This app is perfect for me as a social gamer and a self-improvement fiend. My friends jumped in, and the group motivation to check off our individual habits and to-dos is higher than it could ever be. It's like that African proverb: "If you want to go fast, go alone...if you want to go far, go together." 

If I could make Habitica even better, I'd iron out the bugs (the entire rewards page disappears when I add a new reward, the app crashes for me at least once a day, and sometimes it takes awhile for habits to respond). Also be careful when you're switching between desktop and mobile to make sure the changes you made on either one take effect. But I think this app is doing a great job overall, and if they're committed to the principle of self-improvement that they're purposed for, it could be even more amazing!

I don’t know where anything is, I don’t know what anything does, or what I’m supposed to be doing. User friendliness is slightly better on the website, but that’s a whole lot less convenient to have to get my laptop out just to check off my habits for the day.

This app is a task in itself, which certainly isn’t a good motivator for me to get other tasks done.

title: Honestly changed my life
body:
I have MADD, and the mental illness had practically taken over my whole life. I never got anything done, and I felt my life slipping away a bit. Then I saw this app begging recommended on Tumblr by people who suffered with ADHD; saying it helped them a lot. I don’t believe I have ADHD, but I am video game motivated; so I thought I’d give it a shot. Best. Decision. Of. My. Life!
I have only been using this app for about a month or two, but I already feel my whole life back on track! I feel motivated, productive, and I’m finally getting around to doing all the things I always wanted to do (but never was able to because of my MADD).
This app isn’t for everyone. I would readily admit that. It’s also very simple and basic. I understand some people’s complaints. However, if you have trouble being productive like me, and like video games, I say give it a shot. You have nothing to lose, but everything to gain!

title: Steep learning curve, but fun if you try
body: Originally heard about Habitica (formerly HabitRPG) in 2013. But everything was so confusing to understand. It didn’t even feel like a “game” because I spent the first few days wondering how to input and track my habits. Thankfully they made some UI changes and a new name change. This year I came back to the app and was surprised how fluid the process was. You set up your habits and to dos, join Guilds to socialize with people, and from there form “parties” and go on Quests to defeat monsters by doing your habits. That’s where the social accountability comes into play, and along with the gameified aspect, makes things fun. Hopefully they try making the app easier to navigate. They’ve made a lot of improvements but still have more potential.

title: Amazing App Gets Better!
body:
I downloaded this on a lark, with great cynicism, when it was recently featured in the App Store. 

While other reviews are fairly negative, I’d like to point out the following:

- This is an intuitive and *100% free* to play task and personal organization app. 

- Gamification of daily tasks, habits, and to-do’s is decently executed, with regular updates making the app better all of the time. 

- Development is ongoing and the Dev team seems to value user feedback a lot!

Bottom line for my 5-star rating is that I’ve paid a LOT to crawl through the bitter disappointment of the App Store’s organizational app category. This free app blows that all away and has helped me enact my personal time management goals. I’ve roped in most of my family already and it’s been great for managing house chore lists - we are just getting in to quests, which are a really neat incentive!

As someone with ADHD this is huge, so I highly suggest this for Neurodiverse folks - it’s free so there’s nothing to lose. 

TLDR; download this and give developers your feedback if you have complaints - otherwise it’s free, intuitive, and effective.

One thing that I would love to see in the future would be an Apple Watch version that allows me to just look at the habits, dailies, and todo lists and be able to check them off as I go, instead of having to pull my phone out every time I do something. I highly recommend this app if you like making your regular and irregular tasks fun, like being rewarded for each task completed (no matter how small they are), and want to join a community that is overall very supportive of each other.

title: Awesome tool, awesome community
body:
If you’re a self improvement junkie like I am, you’ll love Habitica. It has all of the habit tracking needs, from tasks that repeat daily, habits you can check at any time, and a to-do list and rewards column that allow you to modify your life as much as you like. 

You can use Habitica as much or as little as you like — some just use it as a simple habit tracker, others go deep and socialize, contribute, and play. There are some lower star ratings on this app because yes, it has been known to be buggy — but my 5 Star is for the community, which (in the true spirit of the app) is full of moderators and staff members who work diligently to improve what’s not working and volunteer contributors who help make Habitica a more rewarding place for everyone.

Honestly, if I weren't head over heels with the concept I would have immediately deleted the app and moved on. I love it SO MUCH and I DESPERATELY want to see it succeed so I want to stick with it and see if the bugs get worked out. Please address these issues because I REALLY want to give it 5 ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️!!!! title: Loved by teenagers & adults at our house
body:
I’m a Mom of six kids born over three decades (ages 2-21). I used to be an avid WoW player since vanilla, but quit now that I have 2 young kids again. I joined Habitica to use my love of video games to motivate me to do the many different things I have to do as a mother, wife, and homemaker.  I also suffer from chronic back & sciatic pain stemming from an L5/S1 herniated disc that has led to 2 surgeries & possibly more, and I've suffered from multiple mental illnesses for years. Habaticia is a sanctuary of kindness & motivation I'm so grateful to have found! It helps keep me accountable when my depression tells me to stay in bed all day, to socialize when my anxiety says to isolate, and to move and do something, anything, when my physical pain is high. I've shown it to my therapist and he highly approves and says he's recommended it to a few other clients! I'm also an autism advocate as 3 of my children are on the spectrum.2-21). I used to be an avid WoW player since vanilla, but quit now that I have 2 young kids again. I joined Habitica to use my love of video games to motivate me to do the many different things I have to do as a mother, wife, and homemaker.  I also suffer from chronic back & sciatic pain stemming from an L5/S1 herniated disc that has led to 2 surgeries & possibly more, and I've suffered from multiple mental illnesses for years. Habaticia is a sanctuary of kindness & motivation I'm so grateful to have found! It helps keep me accountable when my depression tells me to stay in bed all day, to socialize when my anxiety says to isolate, and to move and do something, anything, when my physical pain is high. I've shown it to my therapist and he thinks it’s great for me and has recommended it to other clients.

My teens and I are not only bonding with each other, we are improving our productivity as well.
Anyone ages 13ish up can use this. My teenagers set habits (positive ones to increase & negative ones to decrease), daily must (should) dos, and specific one time only to-dos around school, extracurriculars etc. We are all in a party together and we have friendly competitions about who levels faster etc. It’s silly that collecting every type of online cute pets is motivating enough to get me to clean or teenagers to do homework, but it’s working! We work on quests together it’s great. However you can TOTALLY play by yourself. I played for over three months before getting my family on board, and there are guilds, chats, and challenges anyone can join.
The community is probably the friendliest I’ve EVER seen on the internet, ask a question and you’ll get a friendly answer or pointed in the right direction. No hate, just a group of people looking to improve their real lives through a fun game. Many guilds covering a WIDE multitude of subjects, and challenges you can join to improve yourself further (I.E. I’m currently working on quitting vaping & keeping a cleaner home). Can’t recommend enough! The app does have its glitches, but the website version Habitica.com is near flawless with a very helpful Wiki the site directs you to. You can use the site and app back and forth rather seamlessly.

title: 10/10 IGN
body:
I don’t normally leave reviews, but I feel this app really deserves it.

Habitica, simply put, is a app that takes RPG elements from video games and applies them to real life duties in the form of “Habits,” To-Do’s,” and “Dailies.”  It’s a really interesting and fun concept; I’ve enjoyed it very much so far. I even spent the last hour coming up with achievement-like names for my to-do’s, dailies, and habits. While it wasn’t the most productive thing to do, I sure did get a kick out of it. To add icing to this already delicious cake, the in-app purchases are cosmetic only (as far as I know). Only complaint I have is that the raid boss is too OP. I’m kidding, haha. Kudos to the devs for making this wildly fun yet productive app.

title: If I could bring one app to a desert island...
body:
...it would be Habitica. Ok, it would probably be Netflix or Youtube in all seriousness, but if productivity was more important than entertainment on that desert island, Habitica would be the winner!
Although the app is a little buggy sometimes, I've never had serious issues and there is usually a work- around (often as simple as waiting a few extra seconds for a screen to load). 
Habitica is the only app I open every single day, and I can honestly say it's changed my life. I have a list of about twenty Dailies, several of which are set to only appear on certain days of the week, helping me stick to some sort of daily routine (I didn't regularly brush my teeth, wash my face, or put on facial cream before using Habitica, and now I do them automatically! If that makes me sound like a slob...well, I sure used to be). They serve as reminders for tasks like practicing music, writing journal entries, taking birth control, and my "Big Three"--the three goals I set each day. Homework assignments that are due at the same time each week (like reading questions) are also a great fit for Dailies as they can be set for the day of the week that the recurring task is due. 
As for Habits, I try to curate that list more carefully, since the pressure of maintaining my "streak" isn't there to motivate me to complete them. I keep my list of Habits to 10 or less. They include "drink a glass of water," "write a book review on your blog," "meditate for five minutes," "exercise for fifteen minutes," and "do piano exercises." 
My To-Do list, by the way, is usually filled with Challenge tasks. (I don't create many myself.)
One of my favorite features? I can "dress up" my character using the "costume" feature, and collecting, raising and displaying pets and mounts is really fun, too!
Hope this review motivates you to try Habitica and gives you some ideas for all the different ways you can incorporate it into your life :)

The different guilds and ways to join a party are excellent. They have guilds for everyone and anything. There is a huge and encouraging community here. I highly recommend joining a party to encourage yourself to reach your goals. 

My only quibbles is that the iOS version needs sounds, a widget, and a few tweaks with the UI in regard to finding and input. Also an easier way to invite people would be handy. 

Regardless, I recommend this highly for anyone looking to get motivated.

title: Don’t look anywhere else - HABITICA IS THE BEST!!
body:
Let me ask you a question. Would you rather be tracking your habits with no fun at all - no reward for completing your daily tasks? Or, would you rather obtain habits, daily tasks, and to-do’s but do them in the form of an RPG game, having fun while checking things off of your list? Well, the first option is every other habit tracking app in existence...and the second option is Habitica.

In Habitica, you can add habits, dailies, and to-do’s to your profile. When you complete these things, you gain coins, gems, and health. With coins and gems, you can purchase armor, weapons, pets, etc. These things will help you in quests, whether it’s a collect quest, boss quest, or anything else. You can also join a guild to quest with your best friends.

I love Habitica! I was recommended to it by a friend, and now I’m recommending it to you. It adds that little bit of fun that everyone needs in competing boring tasks that you usually procrastinate through and never get done. I’ve only been using Habitica for a few weeks, and I’ve already noticed TONS of positive differences
in my lifestyle. I realize that I am happier and more productive each day, and every night I go to bed feeling like I got a lot done that day. I definitely recommend this app to EVERYONE. I’m serious. GET HABITICA NOW!!!

title: Love it, but missing something very helpful
body:
This app makes setting and working towards goals easy, fun, and interactive. The only thing I would suggest as improvement would be to add an “Impact” option for each habit. For example, a bad habit that I set as high impact (let’s say smoking) would have a greater effect on my score than a bad habit with a low impact (such as checking email too much). The same with a high impact good habit (saying a prayer) compared to a low impact one (reading an inspiring quote in the morning). These would all have different effects on the score when completed or neglected, thus allowing the user to prioritize which ones to complete at first. 
Hope this suggestion helps :)

I use this app all day long. Habitica has become a core part of my daily routine and in that respect, I love it. The mobile app however has had and continues to have quality problems that make it frustrating to use. The food for pets screen has had shown duplicates and "phantom food" for as long as I can remember, at least a year, probably more. I totally appreciate the energy and I recognize that habitica is largely contribution driven, but if we want a larger community, the tools need to work reliably.

And you get rewarded more if you wait to get things done. So basically you get rewarded for procrastinating. There should be a streak tracker in it or something where you get rewarded more for maintaining a habit, but the rewards drop significantly as soon as you break the habit. There needs to be high reward and high stakes, and if there were, I would reverse this review. Instead, I'm just going to watch my progress grind to a halt and never get to level up because I am actually keeping my habits, which makes is discouraging  rather than habit forming

title: Good idea, poor execution
body: The app is fun. I enjoyed trying to get all of the pets and all of the armor. The task managing is slightly par albeit glitchy. The idea to gamify your to do list is a great one and I loved doing my tasks while I began using this app. However, the pet collecting begins to get old and not worth it once you've gotten them all in about a months time. While the app is a work in progress, I understand there will be some problems. However, in order to do 75% of the advanced things such as purchase gems with gold, change your name, or cancel a subscription, you have to use the website. This basically makes the app useless, as the app is only slightly faster than the website anyways. Customer support is also severely lacking, with one person in charge of the support that checks their emails once a day. There are many better task managers out there (that are also cheaper for a year subscription--ex. Todoist which is ~$30 vs ~$48 Habitica). title: Life changing
body:
Habitica it is absolutely one of the greatest apps I’ve ever used. I feel like video games (especially RPGs) have taught me a lot and helped me to become a productive grownup.

Habitica takes your every day task list and turns it into quests in a 8-bit RPG. The beauty of Habitica is there isn’t really anything to do except what you have to do in your day to day life. For example, you might set up a task “Workout"– When you complete it, you check it off and gain some experience and gold. When you and your friends start a “quest” you fight a monster or boss each night. Depending on how many of your tasks you did or didn’t do, you will damage the boss and/or he will damage you. You can also add bad habits in, like “Eat Donuts”, if you eat a donut, you click it and you will lose some HP that day. You do it yourself, so its basically honor system, but it wouldn’t be much fun if you cheated anyways

I love that each task lets you have a section inside that is a "checklist". This makes it so on the outside you can see "2/10 completed", which helps for larger projects.

title: A+ method to staying on top of things
body:
I've been using this app for well over a year now and I'm still in love.

Perks of habitica:
- keep detailed lists of everything you need to get done, and have them repeat when you want them to.
- the different categories of lists make things SO easy to keep track of. I have flossing under 'habits', making my bed under 'dailies', and then schoolwork goes under 'to do'. It makes it easy for me to prioritize things and go from list to list efficiently.
- The gamer element to this app is what sold me completely. With quests that have mount, pet and item rewards, you feel compelled to collect them all (which I did and STILL feel hooked).
- The party and guild systems are a GREAT way to find similar app users to lightly socialize with and motivate yourself further! 
- On top of all of this, you can access your Habitica from your computer as well as your phone.

Negatives to this app:
- Bugs. Certain patches will sometimes lag or glitch, but this is a big app with many functions...so it's to be expected, but I'd like to see some server performance updates.
- this isn't so much a fault to the app, but I would like to see a button added to completely wipe out my inventory of items, as you just start collecting and hoarding them as you reach higher levels.
- Completely satisfied otherwise!

title: Love the premise & while slightly buggy, also has a lot of potential
body:

I would prefer an overview/abstract of how we're doing on a calendar and will probably fill out a feedback form to request that. As well as somehow adding the ability to set a dailies task that must be completed within, say 4 days, and if you miss the 1st day of that time frame, it doesn't just set it to 4 days later, it allows you 3 more days to finish and when you do complete the task, it'll set another 4-day timespan after - maybe by adding an option for hard deadline/open deadline?
There aren't any bugs that make the app unusable at all. There are a couple currently but they're minimal and don't take away from the usefulness of the app - it's just little dinks here and there like arrangement that bugs, at least in my experience. 
Thanks for such a great app and offering it for free! It's so great that the monetary parts of this app just gives inconsequential in-game purchases that are geared to the game aspect of the app. I don't really use the app as a game but the HP aspect does make me feel motivated to try harder! I'll definitely be purchasing some gems in the future to support the company. :)

title: Awesome Task Manager!
body:
At first I decided to try this app out in helping develop better habits with my email inbox and calling family, but I soon saw how much more this app can help me do.
 I tried a couple other task managers such as Todoist and Any.do before trying Habitica and none of them seemed to give me the features or user interface I wanted in a task manager even before paying for them. These apps sometimes put reminders behind paywalls, or made it cumbersome to set due dates or reminders. These apps also cluttered my list of tasks with other minor tasks I wanted to do eventually and didn't seem to have an unobtrusive or simple way to hide them for later. 
  Habitica on the other side has a simple label options where you can easily set a due date for some and none for others and you can then choose an option where it only shows you those tasks with due dates, puts them in due date order, and hides all other tasks, making the list itself a lot less intimidating. Habitica also offers the option of setting up recurring tasks and lets you choose the intervals from every other day to every month.
  What makes Habitica even more awesome is that they don't hide all of these awesome features behind a paywall, but have it all available in the base version unlike other apps.  
 Even if the idea of role-playing to do chores doesn't really appeal to you, Habitica works so well as a task manager that I'd recommend it to everyone, gamer or not-gamer. 
Awesome App!

title: A party member's #1 pet peeve = vanished!!
body:
So, this app I am just beginning to tap into, since I have made it a slow but deep delving into gamifying my life and that of my family (that's Mama and two lil' ones...), it just corrected my most discerning of reviewers, my son Huxley Charles. 

Huxley said he'd accidentally press the (-) when he meant to press the (+) for habits and so he maintained a disdain for the habits. No matter what I said, he refuted my arguments with this seemingly small issue. 

I want to THANK you a million times over, because now our WHOLE family of three can use all main features. 

This app has changed our lives in the most positive ways. I want to thank my daughter Aurora Delphine because she did a cool thing I thought was meaningless at the start: making learning something new about Habitica a DAILY! We can go to her or communicate with Aurora Delphine, and he will tell us or message us something new every day that is a fantastic tip or trick.

We have very very little money right now, but I still bought gems to support because of the major contributions this program has made. We don't even need to make up our own prizes, though I have tried a little bit with that, because we realy think your avatars and mounts and potions are amazing.

Also, thank you for putting the number of "To-Do's" down in red as the Dailies have had. I have been involved in a few (about three) major projects that require an extraordinary amount of To-Do's and this assists in tempering that down a bit when I updated and saw I had "91", most of them due in the next 24 hours. Is it possible? Yes, I have pushed myself way beyond what I thought I could accomplish using these. And it helps I think to add small To-Do's you know you can get done quickly just to lower the number by three by adding five... if that makes sense! The boost I get self-esteem-wise is incredible.

I would like to thank the various Guilds and topics that encourage a person to turn something banal into something that sounds adventerous. I am currenty working on building the creativity of my dailies by doing this with every daily when it becomes possible.

I just now hooked up to the browser functions because I could no longer stand hearing about challenges and not being able to join them. I must say, the social support is there, the lack of structure as far as how many times you hit a (+) or (-) is there, and that gives you the freedom to judge yourself in a special way. It is helpful when I have to hit the (-) because I did a negative habit, but then based on howstrongly I decided and followed through stopping that habit, I will hit that (+) button. 

I have kept up to date on the research surrounding essential habits, habits that tend to have an effect on all other habits. In Habitica, one need not discover which habits are the essential ones, but simply organize life this way in whatever way suits you, and then you find things will indeed begin to go your wayand more positive habits will begin to domino from having some of the habits be these essential "KEY HABITS". 

I like the new icons; I like it showing the date for Dailies more pronounced there, and I can tell right now that my weekly shuffle of Habits, Dailies, and To-Do's will be a lot easier since the icons make me think of them more properly to begin with. 

I will have more to say once I have explored this more. But to our family, we appreciate the reduction in stress and the increase in the beauty of our bodies, our minds, our home, and our relationships. Even in the furthering of our education individually and as a group, and in the need for more social support from the shyest of us to the most outgoing, it has been ongoing for two days shy of two months STRAIGHT for the three of us: a 9.5 year old boy Huxley Charles, a just turned 12 year old girl Aurora Delphine, and a young Mama who has family and creativity proirities galore, that wuld otherwise BURST at the seams but for gamifying this way.

I will also mention that we are right now using Procraster and I am trying out learning IQTell.. we will have to see which email service is the best for filtering my email down to next to nothing (close to Inbox Zero would be GREAT!) and is the most user-friendly. I want to expand my knowledge of coding but that is through the kids who teach me. I hope we can all contribute to Habitica one day! 

And if anyone know sif I shoudl use a certain email client for Inbox Zero that is linked up with all this.. or a calendar that is Moleskine but is saved somewhere other than just on my devices just in case but JUST as beautiful, or anything from IFTTT that makes a great connection or few here that would maybe connect anything like Procraster but NOT Pomodoro.. only because it blocks things that I don't need bocked and it's nothing like the start screen of Procraster... gosh, I LOVE THAT START SCREEN... how are you feeling about your project? Habitica, Open Source some of that how are you feeling and here are some suggestions stuff!!

Okay, we made a HUGE investment - no joke, we are on disability because I have a serious illness and had to give up my promising career as a top surgeon and - well, at east it led me to filmmaking and such.. but 4.99 per month is a good start.

Also, kudos on partnership with "seeds". I am hoping that this company is not limited to certain countries becaiuse women really need micro-loans everywhere. I will check it out. I love the concept though, and will check out play seeds.com.

More later, sorry so long, we are just REALLY GRATEFUL. Also, we are trying to fund my daughter's trip as a Young Leader to Washington, DC, and we are about 1800 away. We have received about 1200 so far though. So I am looking for these online funding sources and scared to ask for money, but for Aurora Delphine, I will do anything. So, hopefully the social good goes in a circle and I can get past my fear of taking donations for her to attend this summit she was nominated for.

title: Platform for My Life
body:
As what I see as the love child of Fitbit, a classic paper planner, and Pokémon, Habitica has fundamentally improved the way I approach growth in life. It's fun, has an easy and aesthetically pleasing interface, and is both the goal-setting platform and planner I'd been wishing for for years. I've been using it for two years now, and I feel like I am so much more anchored on a day to day basis, I'm more confident in my ability to set and meet goals, and I'm much better at setting realistic goals that don't set me up for failure (and the frustration and self-critique that comes with it.)

Things I love best: 

Having a platform to set long term habit-building goals through the "Habits" and "Dailies" features. (That helps tackle the late-night random thoughts of "I should pick up the violin again" that I used to forget upon falling asleep, only to remember 4 months down the road.)

Keeping track of day to day things with the "To-Do" list (Sure, phone alarms and calendar apps work fine, but I don't get experience points and gold to buy rad armor for my avatar or food for my pet on Google Calendar...😜)

Enjoying the incentives worked into the game to make habit-building fun.(The aforementioned earning gold to buy equipment for my avatar and earning experience to level up notwithstanding, you can join up with friends or members of the incredible community to motivate each other and fight bosses [though you can do this solo too], and maybe my favorite of finding/buying pet eggs with your earned gold to hatch and enjoy as pets or feed to grow into a mounts.)

Many thanks to the incredible team that put together and runs Habitica.

title: Useful but buggy
body:
The concept is brilliant. I love getting points for doing the stuff I want to do. Getting penalized for not doing those things is less fun, but that's kind of the point.

The app is clever but buggy. It frequently reports a "Network Error" even when my Wi-Fi or cell signal is fine. I test the connection with other apps, and they have no trouble. The main problem with this connectivity drop is that offline, the app is useless. Usually apps store your activity and then upload when the connection is restored. But when the app can't connect to the server, you can't so much as tick a to-do item off your list. In this regard, it's often better to use the Habitica website rather than the app.

Another place where the website outdoes the app is in re-ordering lists. In the app, you can ostensibly press and hold an item to drag it to a new place in a list. For example, I like to keep my list of daily tasks in the order in which I do them, e.g., taking my meds in the morning and flossing at night. But this often doesn't stick, and lists get randomly disordered. So I tend to do the sorting on the website instead.

The benefits of using the app do outweigh the annoyance of these bugs. But only because the website makes up for the app's shortcomings.

title: Super fun, and life-changing!!
body:
I cannot say enough good things about Habitica! As someone who has major anxiety and Adult ADD, I've always found staying motivated impossible, and even tiny responsibilities often overwhelming. Habitica turned all of that around! With a clever interface simulating a 16-bit classic RPG, before I knew it I had the positive reinforcement I needed to turn my habits and responsibilities around. 

The goals are 100% customized for what YOU would like to improve about your life, but here's a sampling of my personal turn-arounds that this app has facilitated: my house went from being almost always messy (and kitchen dirty) to being pretty consistently clean, I've started eating better and losing weight, exercising more, getting more sleep, keeping better-informed on world events, saving and keeping better track of my money, and finally starting the process (after several years!) of applying to go back to school. Seriously, it's been a game-changer.

They recommend NOT starting off with goals that are too overwhelming, and I completely agree. As you progress and your character grows, you'll likely naturally want to make a few more life improvements (and get awesome rewards along the way!). Throughout the game you'll level up, eventually get to choose a class, get cool abilities and armor, and find eggs that hatch into a multitude of possible pets, which can often eventually grow into personal steeds!

It gets even better by forming/joining a party with some friends! You'll have help fighting bosses, being buffed by their abilities, and in real life, have even more mutual motivation to stay on top of the things that are important to you!

My only criticisms are that the app does not yet have the full features of the web version, but they are slowly integrating them! And in the meantime, you can always access your account from your phone's Internet to get that extra good
stuff. Still, just about everything you'll need is right there in the app!

I can't give Habitica enough praise. I highly recommend this app to anyone who wants to make some positive changes in their life.

title: Achievement Unlocked: Become a Better Person
body:
I can't say enough how much this app and website have changed my life. For the last few weeks since I got the app, I've been talking about it nearly non-stop... And for good reason. I've struggled for at least 12 years with self discipline and motivation, and no matter what, no organizational apps have been able to keep up with me and my needs. But this is set up perfectly to help me just the way I need. It gives me tangible things to work towards accomplishing, with more of a reward than the sense of accomplishment of checking something off. It helps me to see the progress I've made and break things down into manageable tasks, to sort them in ways that are logical to me, and to take hold of my life day to day as well as in the long term. I've nearly all but broken one of my longest standing bad habits, and the dailies allow me to make sure I'm getting done the small things each day that I might otherwise forget in the midst of a schedule that changes dramatically day to day.

The app doesn't have quite as much functionality as the website, in terms of not having quite as many little goodies, and there are the occasional glitches. But on the whole, the main functionality of the app, where the task management is concerned, functions exactly as it should, and that's what matters the most. I definitely recommend using it concurrent with the website interface, as some of the other aspects function a bit better there. But on the whole? The experience is incredible no matter where you use it.

I'd say this app may not be for everyone, but since starting to use it, I've gotten my family into using it, and they've in turn spread it to their friends... So that's people anywhere from their mid-50s to as young as high school all finding the benefit in it. So maybe it's not for everyone... But I think everyone should at least give it a try before deciding it's not for them, because the appeal is pretty universal.

title: If I could only have one fun app on my phone ...
body:
... I would pick Habitica. 

I downloaded this app before realizing it was the app version of a website. Turned out the website and the app are a terrific combination and have all the tools I needed to start building organization out of chaos. It is great for all ages and all backgrounds. People who want a fun way to keep track of daily habits and increase their productivity will find this useful. Those of us with ADHD will find it life-changing, and there are so many varied groups and communities within the program to lend a positive presence. Interactions and forums are well moderated, graphics are fun, rewards are creative, challenges offer incentives for positive reinforcement, and the community is welcoming and accepting. 

There are a handful of functions that aren't available on the app and must be done from the website, but for the most part, the app does everything I need it to do throughout the day. It even has the direct messaging function now. Truthfully, if I could only have one "fun" app on my phone, this is the one I would keep.

title: Habitica has changed how we do things
body:
Our whole family has been using Habitica for a few months, and it's made a huge difference in how we communicate.  I learned about it in an article about productivity apps and showed it to my 14-year old son, thinking he might be interested in something like this because he likes role-playing games like World of Warcraft.  He was so interested that I agreed to sign up with him.  To my surprise, I love it!  I never thought I'd have so much fun leveling up and collecting pets :)  But the best part is the social interaction - we now talk a lot more as a family about what needs to be done, what each person is working on, and what we want to do next.  We check in with each other every day, if for no other reason than deciding which quest to do next.  And we leave messages for each other in the party chat during the day when we're all off doing our own things.  Our party has expanded to include a few of my son's friends, my sister, and my in-laws.  We're all having a blast - the adults are having as much fun as the kids!  Just for comparison, I was a serious GTD-er before this, using Omnifocus and tickler files.  I still use those things to keep track of projects, but Habitica is so much fun for the smaller things!  I'd underestimated the power of fun in being productive.  And with features like tags, filters, checklists, notes, due dates, and repeating tasks, I can do a lot more with this app than I expected.

Additional note:  For me, the website is easier to navigate and seems like there are more features there, but I am impressed that most things can be done in the app...  I just have to look a little harder to figure out how to do it (like beginning a new quest, for example; it's apparent how to do it on the website, but not as obvious on the app).

Also, kudos to the developers for keeping things so active.  In the mere months we've been using this, there have been multiple app updates, a website update, a world quest (all Habiticans), special sets of seasonal gear and potions (turn your friends into flowers or starfish).  I'm truly impressed with all the details that go into this.  Thank you!

title: This app literally changed my life
body:
I downloaded Habitica because I was having difficulty remembering my plethora of tasks at work. I looked around for task management software and found a few, but nothing really helped. Then I saw Habitica's ad with the rogue and the witch doing homework and yoga, and I downloaded the app immediately. To my delight, it is even better than I was anticipating. To my delight, I take that extra minute to send that last email, because in doing so I receive XP and gold! My productivity has increased drastically, and I no longer forget to complete tasks in my fast-paced work environment. I originally downloaded Habitica thinking it would be something I'd only use at work, but Habitica has also really helped me improve in the realm of self care. I now schedule those doctor's appointments. I reorganized that closet. I cleared out my wardrobe and donated lightly used items. I cooked dinner four out of five nights last week. I floss now. Yes. I floss. I am going to start meditating as a daily. And you know what? I'm actually going to do it. Because I really want to complete my collection of multi-colored, adorable
8-bit pets. I love this app. I recommend it to everyone I know. You won't regret this download. It changed my life.

title: Best GTD system I've found
body: I am a psychotherapist who works with youth facing ADHD and depression and I am promoting this app like crazy. For one, it finally gives socially isolated individuals a reason to take action on things. It's truly entertaining and reaches many who are tired of other people telling them what to do in life and how to do it. With this system, they do what they want for their own edification. That's huge! The second reason I'm promoting this app is because it is the best GTD system I've found for one reason: it is highly customizable to the individual's preference for 1) how to capture potential actions, and 2) how to be rewarded for taking actions. The power of the system is that it pays attention to both habit formation AND task completion. It is the complete behavior modification package. In addition, the game element is undeniably fun though it is never in-your-face and I don't feel childish at all using it. There are some bugs but give them time to work it out: the company is largely supported by an open-source, volunteer community. This is a true mom-and-pop organization. Plus, the app was originally meant to be supplementary to the website (though I haven't had the need to use the website). Speaking of community, the community guidelines ensure the public spaces are family-friendly and kid-appropriate. The website and app are most helpful when users interact with other community members, though this isn't necessary to enjoy the app and it may take some users time to feel safe enough. The community is very friendly to newcomers and all questions can be answered in the Tavern and guilds. TL;DR Best GTD system I've found because it's based on science and supported by a generous and kind community.

title: Beautiful and effective
body:
I never write reviews for apps, but I've been inspired. I've been an avid ToDoist user for over a year, but when my premium membership expired I acquiesced to my husband's longstanding request to join his Habitica team. RPGs really aren't my thing, and I honestly couldn't care less about the actual game aspect, but the organizational scheme, point system, and ability to generate your own rewards are features that are worthwhile on their own. Turning it into a game just gives you one more reason to actually use it!

I started with Habitica's desktop platform. I haven't had the best luck with list-based apps, so I was extremely skeptical when I downloaded it, but this is a beautiful and well organized interface. I will definitely continue using this app, and may even let go of the other to-do apps on my phone (I'm a business owner and a to-do list junkie). It's better than any of my paid apps. I can't believe it's free!

I made tasks for all sorts of things. Self care, taking my medications, and even positive affirmations for my anxiety. This app has been so great for my mood I've actually started doing chores around the house again. I really feel like I'm getting better control of my depression for the first time in my life. I'm so thankful for this app. I get rewards for spending time with friends, petting animals, or spending time with my boyfriend. If you suffer from any mental illness, or know someone who does, I recommend this. It's a game changer!

author: Cati.ben

title: Awesome to do app
body:
This might be the coolest to do app I've seen. Completing tasks earns you gold and experience points to level up your little avatar. You can set up three types of tasks: habits (for positive/negative feedback), dailies (which you must complete in the specified time frame or they will cause you to lose health), and to do (which can be set with a due date or not). Tasks can have subtasks. You get to determine how difficult each task is, and you are rewarded/punished accordingly.

I gave it four stars because it is a little buggy (nothing that's interfered with using the app so far, just visual things). Also To Do tasks can't be set to repeat, which I could very much use.

title: Good redesign but needs fixes
body:
Love the new redesign! Looks very nice, flows well. As an iPhone user, however, I have a few big interface complaints which need tending:
-Drop down notifications within the app are very large, slow, and obtrusive. They cannot be dismissed, either, so multiple notifications (r.g. on login) are really annoying and interfere with use of the app.
-Scroll, scroll, scroll! Most interface list items take up way too much vertical space due to huge colored areas. This makes the app very inefficient when working with multiple items and prevents seeing more than two tasks at a time.
-Party and skills are buried in an irritating catch-all tab on the far right. Perhaps allow users to control which bottoms show on the bottom.
-Network lagginess. Combined with the aforementioned slow notification speed, makes using the app painful at times. Half the time, spell selection doesn't even do anything. Try logging in and casting two spells. See how long it takes!

title: I don't write reviews.
body:
I want to play this game. I REALLY want to play this. However it is extremely difficult to get into. Unless I'm fundamentally missing something to do ANYTHING rewarding in this app you have to be in a party, level 15, or buy a quest scroll. This makes the game very inaccessible to me, as my friends wouldn't be interested. That means I have to stick with this game long enough to get to level 15 before I can have fun with it. Are you kidding me? A good game design would get me hooked from the get go, THEN make me feel like I need to do real work to progress. 

For example what if the game started with a short play section. Perhaps a battle or an introduction sequence. Make it fun, I don't even know what I'm working towards. There's no reward that I see within my grasp. Oh coins? Uh... Okay. That I can buy weapons and gear with... Oooookay. To fight.. What? Why do I want this stuff? Why am I putting forth effort into this game? The concept is good but please designers, make me want it. You're giving me nothing.

title: Excellent for building or breaking habits
body:
For anyone who has played rpg's, Habitica is a great habit building app. The app reminds you to finish your dailies, which cause your character to lose health if skipped. It basically guilts you into accomplishing your goals and rewards you in a way that's easy to see.

All habits, dailies, and to-do's are customizable. The harder you set the habit to, the more experience you will gain from accomplishing it.

I will note that if you have been a member and are returning to the game, do NOT reset your account. At least don't reset it if you have limited edition items. Back when it was HabitRPG I signed up but didn't do much with it. I cam back recently and I had two awesome mounts for being a member. Without considering where the mounts came from, I reset my account thinking it would be good to get a fresh start. I lost the mounts (of course).

title: Beautiful new interface to a great tool!
body:
Using HabitRPG has helped me improve my life.  I didn’t “get it” the first time I uploaded to, because thought of it as  a “to do” list.  It is much more than that.  For one thing, it’s helped me understand how I can make the changes I want to make in my life, and what keeps me motivated to do so.  It is a very flexible, intelligently conceived RPG that can become an essential tool to improve your life incrementally, and permanently.  

This new version is handsome, clear and a pleasure to use.  I love the new icon.  I had never thought of myself as a role play gamer, so the new name and icon feel more inclusive to me.  I prefer apps that have a sleek, visual appeal that this new app has.

To new users, be aware that the learning curve, even with the help of the tutorials, thoughtful game structure and excellent wiki, is still steep.  Not nearly as steep as OmniFocus, but much, much more effective, and much easier to use on a daily basis.  Start small and easy.  Get some wins.  If you get addicted, it will be to your own health and to the development of beneficial habits.

When you start using this app, you can (but do not have to) become part of a larger community of people trying to get things done, overcome bad habits or start good ones.  I’ve found this community to be very supportive and generous.  

Get this app, start using it, and support the brilliant, hard working developers.
